ITQAN:v2p415/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p415/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p415/r12.claim: Dhikr can refer to the Preserved Tablet.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r3.claim: The conclusion reassures the Prophet and companions that all prophets taught one message; they should persist and leave those who divided it to God, since late faith will not help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r3.anchor: all prophets of God have taught the same message they are preaching

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r4.claim: Only God's pious servants attain the Hereafter's success; judgement is near, and the Prophet ends by supplicating God to judge between him and his foes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r4.anchor: a decisive declaration is made from the tongue of the Prophet (sws) that the time of judgement is at hand

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p155/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p155/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p155/r9.claim: The verse refers to the Psalms, whose chapter 37 focuses especially on the earth being inherited by God's righteous servants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p155/r9.anchor: This verse refers to the Psalms.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r1.claim: Psalm 37 is especially devoted to the promise that God's righteous servants inherit the earth, supporting the Qur'an's reference.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r2.claim: The author reproduces Psalm 37 in full to show which 'earth' the verse means and clarify its allusion and wording.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r2.anchor: becomes clear which “earth” is being referred to here.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r3.speaker: Psalms
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r3.claim: Psalm 37 contrasts the wicked, who wither and are destroyed, with those who trust in the Lord and inherit the land; the meek enjoy peace there.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p156/r3.anchor: those who are evil will be destroyed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p157/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p157/r1.speaker: Psalms
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p157/r1.claim: Psalm 37 reiterates that the righteous inherit and dwell in the land forever, God protects the faithful, and the wicked and their offspring perish.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p158/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p158/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p158/r1.claim: Islahi identifies the Qur’anic allusion as Psalm 37, whose discrete stanzas pair counsel with a repeated promise that the pious inherit the land.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p158/r1.anchor: discrete stanzas in which words of counsel are sounded first and then a repetitive verse occurs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p158/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p158/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p158/r2.claim: The promised inheritance cannot mean the present earth: it is mortal, and God gives respite there to both righteous and wicked people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p158/r2.anchor: this earth and all of its things are mortal and God has given respite in it to both the righteous and the wicked

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r1.claim: The Psalm’s eternal inheritance concerns the Hereafter: the present sky and earth will be destroyed and replaced by a new world for the righteous, as Qur’an 21:104 and 14:48 indicate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r1.anchor: Earlier in verse 104, it is pointed out that one day the Almighty will destroy this sky.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r2.claim: The new earth and sky will belong eternally to the righteous; wrongdoers will have no share and will be cast into Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r2.anchor: they will eternally belong to the righteous. The wrongdoers will have no share in it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r3.claim: Islahi notes that the Psalms are hymns revealed to David, a prophet and illustrious king, making his proclamation of the final righteous kingdom especially forceful.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r3.anchor: a prophet as well as an illustrious king.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r4.claim: The Qur’anic allusion recalls the Psalm’s moving elaboration and repeated promise, preceded by counsel; Islahi says this counsel guarantees the eternal kingdom in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p159/r4.anchor: it is these words of counsel which guarantee an eternal kingdom in the Hereafter.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r2.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says الزبور is David's Psalms and that the verse's meaning is present there and was read in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r2.anchor: والزبور الظاهر أنه زبور داود وقاله الشعبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies الذكر as the Torah.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes الزبور the books revealed after the Torah while retaining الذكر as the Torah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r4.anchor: وقيل الزبور ما بعد التوراة من الكتب والذكر التوراة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r5.claim: A further interpretation takes الزبور to encompass all revealed books and الذكر to mean the Preserved Tablet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r5.anchor: وقيل الزبور يعم الكتب المنزلة والذكر اللوح المحفوظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets الأرض as the land of Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r6.anchor: الأرض قال ابن عباس أرض الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r7.claim: Another view identifies it as the Holy Land, to be inherited by Muhammad's community.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p472#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: الأرض المقدسة يرثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

JISHUMI:v7p4900/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r3.claim: The phrase “after the Reminder” shows that the Zabur is created, since it came after the Reminder.
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: (من بعد الذكر) أن الزبور محدث؛ لأنه بعد الذكر.

JISHUMI:v7p4900/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r4.claim: God wrote these matters as a benefit for the angels.
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r4.anchor: وتدل على أنه كتب لطفا للملائكة هذه الأشياء.

JISHUMI:v7p4900/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r5.claim: The inheritance of the earth means Paradise is entered by the righteous, not unbelievers or grave sinners, unlike worldly blessings.
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r5.anchor: ويدل قوله: (أن الأرض يرثها) أن الجنة يدخلها الصالح دون الكافر والفاسق،

JISHUMI:v7p4900/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r6.claim: The Quran suffices for those who reflect, refuting the Imami claim that religious guidance requires an Imam.
JISHUMI:v7p4900/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن في القرآن كفاية لمن تدبره، فيبطل قول الإمامية في الحاجة إلى الإمام في الدين.

NAHHAS:v3p82/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p82/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p82/r1.claim: Zabūr and kitāb both mean a written book; Torah and Gospel can therefore be called zabūr, from the verb “I wrote.”
NAHHAS:v3p82/r1.anchor: والزبور والكتاب واحد فلذلك جاز أن يقال للتوراة والإنجيل زبور من زبرت أي كتبت

NAHHAS:v3p82/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p82/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p82/r2.claim: The plural zubur derives from zabartu; whoever says zabūr treats it as the plural of zubr.
NAHHAS:v3p82/r2.anchor: وجمعه زبر ومن قال زبور جعله جمع زبر

NAHHAS:v3p82/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p82/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p82/r3.claim: The best interpretation is that the land inherited by God’s righteous servants is the land of Paradise, since righteous and others have inherited earthly lands.
NAHHAS:v3p82/r3.anchor: أحسن ما قيل فيه أنه يراد بها أرض الجنة لأن الأرض التي في الدنيا قد ورثها الصالحون وغيرهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r1.claim: Zabūr means the revealed books given to the prophets, while al-dhikr is God's heavenly Mother Book.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r1.anchor: أن الزبور الكتب التي أنزلها الله تعالى على أنبيائه , والذكر أم الكتاب الذي عنده في السماء , وهذا قول مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r2.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r2.claim: Zabūr means the revealed books sent to prophets after Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r2.anchor: أن الزبور من الكتب التي أنزلها الله تعالى على من بعد موسى من أنبيائه , وهذا قول الشعبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r3.claim: The righteous who inherit the earth are the people of obedience inheriting Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r3.anchor: أنها أرض الجنة يرثها أهل الطاعة , وهذا قول سعيد بن جبير , وابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r4.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r4.claim: The inherited land is the holy land, inherited by the Children of Israel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r4.anchor: أنها الأرض المقدسة يرثها بنو إسرائيل , وهذا قول الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r5.claim: The inherited land is this world, inherited by Muhammad's community.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p474/r5.anchor: أنها أرض الدنيا , والذي يرثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم , وهذا قول ابن عباس

TABRISI:21:104-112/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-112/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:21:104-112/r1.claim: One interpretation identifies the inherited earth as the familiar earthly realm, conquered by Muhammad's community after unbelievers are expelled.
TABRISI:21:104-112/r1.anchor: هي الأرض المعروفة يرثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالفتوح بعد إجلاء الكفار

TABRISI:21:104-112/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-112/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:21:104-112/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was shown the earth's eastern and western regions and his community's dominion would reach them.
TABRISI:21:104-112/r2.anchor: زويت لي الأرض فأريت مشارقها ومغاربها وسيبلغ ملك أمتي ما زوي لي منها

TABRISI:21:104-112/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-112/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:21:104-112/r3.claim: Abu Jafar identifies the inheritors as the companions of the Mahdi at the end of time, citing reports that a righteous man from the Prophet's family fills earth with justice.
TABRISI:21:104-112/r3.anchor: هم أصحاب المهدي ع في آخر الزمان ويدل على ذلك ما رواه الخاص والعام عن النبي

TABRISI:21:104-112/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-112/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله الحافظ
TABRISI:21:104-112/r4.claim: Al-Hakim calls Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Jundi unknown and notes conflicting chains, including a path through abandoned Aban ibn Abi Ayyash and a disconnected report; he considers Mahdi reports sounder and explicit about the Prophet's family.
TABRISI:21:104-112/r4.anchor: ومحمد بن خالد رجل مجهول واختلف عليه في إسناده

TABRISI:21:104-112/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-112/r5.speaker: محمد بن خالد الجندي
TABRISI:21:104-112/r5.claim: A report attributed through Anas says affairs and miserliness worsen, the Hour comes only upon wicked people, and there is no Mahdi except Jesus; al-Hakim questions its narrator and chains.
TABRISI:21:104-112/r5.anchor: لا يزداد الأمر إلا شدة ولا الناس إلا شحا ولا الدنيا إلا إدبارا

TABRISI:21:106-108/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:106-108/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:21:106-108/r1.claim: The Prophet says that if only one day remained, God would prolong it until a righteous man from his family filled earth with justice.
TABRISI:21:106-108/r1.anchor: لو لم يبق من الدنيا إلا يوم واحد لطول الله ذلك اليوم حتى يبعث فيه رجلا مني أو من أهل بيتي

TABRISI:21:106-108/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:106-108/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:21:106-108/r2.claim: A variant says the Mahdi's name matches the Prophet's and he fills earth with equity after it was filled with injustice.
TABRISI:21:106-108/r2.anchor: يواطىء اسمه اسمي يملأ الأرض قسطا وعدلا كما ملئت ظلما وجورا

TABRISI:21:106-108/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:106-108/r3.speaker: أم سلمة
TABRISI:21:106-108/r3.claim: Umm Salama reports the Prophet saying the Mahdi is from his descendants, from Fatima's children.
TABRISI:21:106-108/r3.anchor: المهدي من عترتي من ولد فاطمة

THALABI:v6p313/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p313/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p313/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the earth in worldly life will belong to believers; the verse promises the religion's manifestation, the Muslims' triumph, and the disbelievers' subjugation.
THALABI:v6p313/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أراد أن الأرض في الدنيا تصير للمؤمنين، وهذا حكم من الله سبحانه بإظهار الدين وإعزاز المسلمين

THALABI:v6p313/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p313/r2.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v6p313/r2.claim: Wahb says he read in several divine books that God will bequeath the earth to the righteous servants of Muhammad's community.
THALABI:v6p313/r2.anchor: قال وهب: قرأت في عدة من كتب الله أن الله عز وجل قال: إني لأورث الأرض عبادي الصالحين من أمة محمد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r5.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r5.claim: Al-Zabur refers to the revealed books that came after the Torah.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r5.anchor: قيل: في الكتب المنزلة بعد التوراة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r6.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r6.claim: Alternatively, al-dhikr means the Preserved Tablet.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r7.claim: The earth that God's righteous servants inherit is the earth of Paradise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r7.anchor: أن الأرض } يعني: أرض الجنة { يرثها عبادي الصالحون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r8.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r8.claim: Alternatively, this means the earthly world will pass to believers from Muhammad's community.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:104-107/r8.anchor: وقيل: أرض الدنيا تصير للمؤمنين من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

SAMIN-DURR:21:105/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:105/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:105/r1.claim: من بعد الذكر can attach to كتبنا or directly to الزبور, understood as the written text.
SAMIN-DURR:21:105/r1.anchor: لأنه بمعنى المزبور أي: المكتوب أي: المزبور من بعد.

SAMIN-DURR:21:105/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:105/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:105/r2.claim: The object of كتبنا is the clause beginning أن; the meaning is that God decreed the righteous would inherit the earth.
SAMIN-DURR:21:105/r2.anchor: ومفعول " كتبنا " أن وما في حيزها أي: كتبنا وراثة الصالحين للأرض أي: حكمنا به.

ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r5.claim: الزبور can collectively mean the revealed books, including Torah, Gospel, and Furqan; زبور and كتاب are synonyms, as are زبرت and كتبت.
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r5.anchor: الزبور: جميع الكتب، التوراة، والإنجيل، والفرقان، زبور، لأن الزبور والكتاب بمعنى واحد.

ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r6.claim: The writing in the books follows God's remembrance or record of it in Heaven.
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r6.anchor: ويقال زبرت وكتبت بمعنى واحد، والمعنى: ولقد كتبنا في الكتب من بعد ذكرنا في السماء

ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r7.speaker: قيل في التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r7.claim: One interpretation identifies the inherited land as Paradise, supported by the description of believers inheriting Firdaws in 23:10–11.
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r7.anchor: قيل في التفسير إنها أرض الجنة، ودليل هذا القول قوله: (أولئك هم الوارثون

ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r8.claim: Zajjaj prefers the known earthly land: when unqualified, الأرض denotes the earth people know, as in 57:1 and the inheritance of the oppressed in 7:137.
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r8.anchor: وقيل إن الأرض ههنا يعنى بها أرض الدنيا، وهذا القول أشبه - كما قال الله عز وجل:

ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r9.claim: Jurists count this verse among their strongest proofs that land is not governed like other property that can be cultivated.
ZAJJAJ:v3p406#2/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية من أجل شواهد الفقهاء أن الأرض ليس مجراها مجرى سائر ما يعمر.

ASAD-NOTES:21:105/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:105/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:105/r1.claim: God had declared in books of divine wisdom that His righteous servants would inherit the earth.
ASAD-NOTES:21:105/r1.anchor: We laid it down in all the books of divine wisdom that My righteous servants shall inherit the earth

ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n100/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n100/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n100/r1.claim: Dhikr literally means “the reminder”; Asad points to 21:10 for its deeper Qur'anic implications.
ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n100/r1.anchor: Lit., "after the reminder (adh-dhikr)". For the deeper implications of the Qur'anic term dhikr

ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n101/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n101/r1.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n101/r1.claim: Tabari treats zabur, literally scripture or book, as a generic term for any book of wisdom and thus for every divine scripture revealed to prophets.
ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n101/r1.anchor: any and all of the divine scriptures revealed by God to the prophets [Tabari]

ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n101/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n101/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n101/r2.claim: The promise that the righteous inherit the earth echoes 3:139: faith and righteous conduct let humanity reach the heights intended by the Creator's grace.
ASAD-NOTES:21:105#n101/r2.anchor: is obviously an echo of the promise, "You are bound to rise high if you are (truly] believers"

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p264#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p264#2/r1.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p264#2/r1.claim: Hamza alone reads al-zabūr with ḍamma on zāy; the other readers use fatḥa, and the author refers back to an earlier discussion.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p431/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p431/r2.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p431/r2.claim: Ḥamza alone uses ḍamma on zāy in الزبور; the others use fatḥa.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p431/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحده ﴿ في الزبور ﴾ بضم الزاى والباقون بفتح الزاى

IBNMUJAHID:v1p432/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p432/r4.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p432/r4.claim: Ḥamza alone leaves yāʾ in عبادي الصالحون still; the others open it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p432/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وحده / عبادى الصلحون / ساكنة الياء وفتحها الباقون

NASHR:v2p324/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p324/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p324/r4.claim: The author refers back to the previously discussed reading of الزبور for Ḥamza and Khalaf in al-Nisāʾ.
NASHR:v2p324/r4.anchor: وتقدم الزبور لحمزة وخلف في النساء

NASHR:v2p324/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p324/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p324/r11.claim: Ḥamza reads the possessive yāʾ in عبادي الصالحون with sukūn.
NASHR:v2p324/r11.anchor: مسني الضر عبادي الصالحون أسكنها حمزة

QIRAAT-ER:21:105:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:21:105:6#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:21:105:6#1/r1.claim: With ḍamma on zāy, al-Zubūr is plural “scriptures/writings,” referring collectively to revealed scriptures rather than specifically to the Psalms.
QIRAAT-ER:21:105:6#1/r1.anchor: vw, mutawatir: "Vowel shift: fatḥa→ḍamma on zāy — al-Zubūri (with ḍamma) = plural ""the scriptures/writings

QIRAAT-ER:21:105:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:21:105:13#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:21:105:13#1/r1.claim: The shortened possessive yāʾ has sukūn rather than the standard fatḥa; this changes the sound but not the meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:21:105:13#1/r1.anchor: Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Variant reading: ʿibādī with sukūn on the yāʾ (shortened) vs standard ʿibādiya with fatḥa

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the Zabur mentioned here came after the Torah.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r1.anchor: معمر عن الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر ﴾ قال في الزبور من بعد التوراة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r2.speaker: غير الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r2.claim: Authorities other than al-Kalbi take the Zabur as the Book and understand the Reminder as the original record kept with God.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r2.anchor: وقال غير الكلبي في الزبور في الكتاب من بعد الذكر قال الأصل الذي عند الله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r3.claim: Qatada reports that when the Prophet attended a battle, he would pray: Lord, judge with truth.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p30#4/r3.anchor: عن قتادة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا شهد قتالا قال رب احكم بالحق

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r1.claim: The apparent meaning of al-Zabur is David's psalm; al-Sha'bi is also reported to identify it this way.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنه زبور داود عليه السلام وروي ذلك عن الشعبي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report from Ibn Jarir, takes al-Zabur as the scriptures and al-Dhikr as the Torah; al-Dahhak is also reported to interpret Dhikr as the Torah.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس أنه الكتب والذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r3.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jubayr identifies Dhikr as the Torah and al-Zabur as the Qur'an.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن جبير أن الذكر التوراة والزبور القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd takes al-Zabur as the books revealed to the prophets and al-Dhikr as the Preserved Tablet, the primordial Mother Book in which things were written beforehand.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r4.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن زيد أن الزبور الكتب التي أنزلت على الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj chooses the interpretation of al-Dhikr as the Mother Book or Preserved Tablet; calling it Dhikr is figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r5.anchor: واختار تفسيره بذلك الزجاج وإطلاق الذكر عليه مجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r6.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r6.claim: A hadith in al-Bukhari says God existed with nothing before Him, His Throne was over water, then He created the heavens and Earth and wrote everything in al-Dhikr; al-Alusi cites it in support of the term for the primordial record.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r6.anchor: وقد وقع في حديث البخاري عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان الله تعالى ولم يكن قبله شيء وكان عرشه على الماء ثم خلق

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r7.claim: The root zabara denotes writing heavily; al-Zabur originally means any densely written book, with the verb's bāʾ read with either fatḥa or ḍamma, as recorded in al-Muhkam.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r7.anchor: وأصل الزبور كل كتاب غليظ الكتابة من زبرت الكتاب أزبر بفتح الموحدة وضمها كما في المحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r8.claim: In common usage al-Zabur is restricted to the revealed book of David.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r8.anchor: وخص في المشهور بالكتاب المنزل على داود عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r9.claim: Some scholars use al-Zabur for a book limited to intellectual wisdom and lacking legal rulings, explaining why David's revelation is called this.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : هو اسم للكتاب المقصور على الحكمة العقلية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r10.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r10.claim: Al-Alusi regards al-Zabur as apparently an Arabic name, permitting min baʿdihi to attach to it or to katabna; Hamza says the name is Syriac.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r10.anchor: والظاهر أنه اسم عربي بمعنى الزبور ولذا جوز تعلق ( من بعده ) به كما جوز تعلقه بكتبنا وقال حمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r11.claim: If al-Zabur means scriptures collectively, the definite article is generic.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#2/r11.anchor: فإذا أريد منه الكتب كان اللام فيه للجنس أي كتبنا في جنس الزبور

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, also reported from Mujāhid, Ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrima, al-Suddī, and Abū al-ʿĀliya, identifies the earth as Paradise, created especially for the righteous.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن المراد بالأرض أرض الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī supports Paradise as the referent: the righteous were created for it, others enter only in their train, and after resurrection it is their sole settled home and divine favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r2.anchor: وإنها الأرض التي يخاص بها الصالحون لأنها لهم خلقت وغيرهم إذا حصلوا فيها فعلى وجه التبع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r3.claim: An alternate report from Ibn ʿAbbās, also held by al-Kalbī, takes the earth as this world, which believers will inherit and possess; it is supported by the promise of succession.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r3.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن المراد بها أرض الدنيا يرثها المؤمنون

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r4.speaker: ثوبان
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r4.claim: Thawbān reports the Prophet saying God folded the earth for him, showed him its eastern and western reaches, and his community's dominion would reach what was folded for him; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r4.anchor: وأخرج مسلم وأبو داود والترمذي عن ثوبان قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تعالى زوى لي الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī reads the report as a promise that God will manifest the religion, honor its adherents, and give them control of most of the inhabited, well-traveled world.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r5.anchor: وهذا وعد منه تعالى بإظهار الدين وإعزاز أهله واستيلائهم على أكثر المعمورة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r6.claim: The promise need not mean believers have reached every land; the New World and western India are examples, unless all lands come under believers in the days of the Mahdī and Jesus.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r6.anchor: وإلا فمن الأرض مالم يطأها المؤمنون كالأرض الشهيرة بالدنيا الجديدة وبالهند الغربي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r7.claim: Another interpretation identifies the inherited earth as the Holy Land.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r8.claim: A further interpretation identifies the inherited earth as Syria.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r8.anchor: وقيل : الشأم ولعل بقاء الكفار وحدهم في الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r9.claim: The unbelievers' sole possession of the earth at the end of time does not negate this inheritance: the brief interval between that state and the Hour is not counted as independent possession.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r9.anchor: ولعل بقاء الكفار وحدهم في الأرض جميعها في آخر الزمان كما صحت به الأخبار لا يضر في هذه الوراثة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers Paradise, the majority interpretation, because it best fits the immediate context.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r10.anchor: والأولى أن تفسر الأرض بأرض الجنة كما ذهب إليه الأكثرون وهو أوفق بالمقام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r11.claim: The famous story that Ibn Kamāl decoded this verse as a prophecy of Sultan Selim's conquest of Egypt came true only by coincidence and is not reliable evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p103#3/r11.anchor: ومن الغرائب قصة تفاؤل السلطان سليم بهذه الآية حين أضمر محاربته للغورى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r11.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid say the Psalter means all revealed books, while the Reminder is the Mother of the Book with God; the sense is that it had already been written in the Preserved Tablet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r11.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد: الزبور جميع الكتب المنزلة، والذكر أم الكتاب الذي عنده، والمعنى من بعد ما كتب ذكره في اللوح المحفوظ.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify the Psalter as the Torah and the Reminder as scriptures revealed after the Torah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك: الزبور التوراة والذكر الكتب المنزلة من بعد التوراة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r13.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r13.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the Psalter is David’s book and the Reminder is the Torah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r13.anchor: وقال الشعبي: الزبور كتاب داود، [والذكر التوراة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r14.claim: Another view identifies the Psalter as David’s Psalms and the Reminder as the Qur’an.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r14.anchor: وقيل: الزبور زبور داود] (2) والذكر القرآن،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r15.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r15.claim: Here بعد means ‘before,’ as illustrated by 18:97 and the statement that the earth was spread after that in 79:30.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r15.anchor: وبعد بمعنى قبل، كقوله تعالى: {وكان وراءهم ملك} (الكهف: 97) : أي أمامهم 23/أ {والأرض بعد ذلك دحاها} (النازعات: 30) قبله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r16.claim: The earth that will be inherited means the land of the Garden.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r17.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r17.claim: Mujāhid identifies the righteous servants as the community of Muhammad.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p358/r17.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r1.claim: A report says the Qur'an raises some people and lowers others; al-Baghawī identifies it as ṣaḥīḥ, transmitted by Muslim from Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r1.anchor: أقواما ويضع به آخرين" صحيح أخرجه مسلم عن زهير بن حرب (1) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet saying that a person with no Qur'an inside is like a ruined house; al-Tirmidhī calls the report ṣaḥīḥ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الرجل الذي ليس في جوفه شيء من القرآن كالبيت الخرب "

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r3.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r3.claim: Wāthila ibn al-Asqaʿ reports that the Prophet received the seven long sūras in place of the Torah, the miʾūn for the Gospel, the mathānī for the Psalms, al-Fātiḥa and the ends of al-Baqara from beneath the Throne, and al-Mufaṣṣal as an extra; al-Baghawī calls it gharīb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41/r3.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " أعطيت مكان التوراة السبع الطوال، وأعطيت مكان الإنجيل المئين، وأعطيت مكان الزبور المثاني،

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r2.claim: Al-dhikr may be the Torah; alternatively, Zabūr means revealed books generally and al-dhikr the Preserved Tablet.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r2.anchor: أي التوراة، وقيل المراد ب { الزبور } جنس الكتب المنزل

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r3.claim: The earth to be inherited may be the Garden or the Holy Land.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r3.anchor: أي أرض الجنة أو الأرض المقدسة

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r4.claim: The righteous heirs may mean all believers, the formerly oppressed who inherit the world's east and west, or Muhammad's community.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:105/r4.anchor: يعني عامة المؤمنين أو الذين كانوا يستضعفون مشارق الأرض ومغاربها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r9.claim: The inheritance promise resumes the connection to the earlier declaration that the revealed Book contains the community's reminder, and recalls God's promise through David.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r9.anchor: عاطفا على { لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r10.claim: The Zabur here is the scripture revealed to David; “after the reminder” means after the opening calls to God, admonitions, glorification, and praise that begin it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r10.anchor: الذي أنزلناه على داود عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r11.claim: “The earth” means the whole category of lands, including the worldly regions, the gathering place, Paradise, and other lands known to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r11.anchor: أي جنسها الشامل لبقاع أرض الدنيا كلها ولأرض المحشر والجنة وغير ذلك مما يعلمه الله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r12.claim: Their possessive link to God marks the servants' distinction; the righteous adopt the people of remembrance's character, turn to God, affirm His oneness, fear the Hour and His might, hope for His mercy, and humble themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r12.anchor: أي المتخلفون بأخلاق أهل الذكر , المقبلين على ربهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r13.claim: The prophets' stories in this sura witness that the final outcome belongs to those who please God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p116/r13.anchor: دلالة على أن العاقبة لمن ارضانا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r1.claim: Biqaʿi links the promise to Quranic assurances that God destroys oppressors and grants the land to chosen servants, and that believers inherit Paradise.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r1.anchor: إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده

BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r2.claim: The promise foretells that this comparatively weak community will inherit what David and Solomon received despite their great power over iron, wind, and animals of every kind.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r2.anchor: وفي هذا إشارة بالبشارة بأنه تعالى يورث هذه الأمة على ضعفها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r3.claim: Biqaʿi takes the promise in its apparent sense because the Zabur begins with remembrances and admonitions and repeats the same wording in Psalm 36 before its fourth section.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r3.anchor: والمراد بهذا الكلام - والله أعلم - ظاهره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r4.claim: Psalm 1 depicts the righteous as avoiding the wicked, delighting in divine law and flourishing like a watered tree, while the wicked are chaff, fail in judgment, and perish.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r4.anchor: طوبى للرجل الذي لا يتبع رأي المنافقين , ولم يقف في طريق الخاطئين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r5.claim: Psalm 2 describes nations and rulers conspiring against God and His anointed, God enthroning His king in Zion and promising him the nations and earth's ends, then warning rulers to serve Him and blessing those who trust Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r5.anchor: لماذا ارتجت الشعوب ؟ وهدت الأمم بالباطل ؟ قامت ملوك الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r6.claim: Psalm 5 presents a morning plea for an answer and guidance: God rejects evil and falsehood, while the speaker enters His temple through mercy and asks for a just path before enemies.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p117/r6.anchor: استمع يارب قولي داعيا , وكن لدعائي مجيبا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r1.claim: Psalm 5 continues that God rejects hypocrites who anger Him, while those who trust Him rejoice, receive blessing, and are surrounded by His favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r1.anchor: ومثل كثرة نفاقهم ارفضهم لأنهم أسخطوك يا رب ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r2.claim: Psalm 6 pleads for mercy rather than angry rebuke, describes bodily pain and tearful nights, says the dead cannot praise God, and trusts that God has heard and will shame the enemies.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r2.anchor: يارب ! لا تبكتني بغضبك , ولا تؤدبني بزجرك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r3.claim: Psalm 9 thanks God for wonders and for defeating enemies, destroying the wicked, and judging the world and its peoples with justice.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r3.anchor: أشكرك يا رب من كل قلبي , وأقص جميع عجائبك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r4.claim: Psalm 12 laments feeling forgotten and threatened by enemies, but trusts God's mercy, rejoices in salvation, and promises to sing to Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r4.anchor: حتى متى يا رب تنساني ألى التمام ؟ حتى متى يارب تصرف وجهك عني

BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r5.claim: Psalm 14 describes the one fit to dwell in God's sanctuary: blameless, truthful, harmless to neighbors, honoring the God-fearing, keeping promises, and refusing interest or bribes.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r5.anchor: يا رب من يسكن في مسكنك أو من يحل في طور قدسك ؟

BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r6.claim: Psalm 16 asks God to hear a just and truthful petitioner, who says God examined him without finding wrongdoing and asks protection from adversaries under God's wings.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p118/r6.anchor: استمع يا الله ببري , وانظر إلى تواضعي , وأنصت لصلاتي من شفتين غير غاشتين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r1.claim: Psalm 16 continues by asking God to rescue the speaker from hypocrites and enemy weapons and to scatter and divide the opponents.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r1.anchor: أدركهم وعرقلتهم , ونج نفسي من ا لمنافقين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r2.claim: Psalm 17 praises God as strength and refuge: the speaker cries amid mortal danger, God hears from His temple, and earthquakes, fire, storm, thunder, and lightning accompany divine intervention.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r2.anchor: المزمور السابع عشر : أحبك يا رب قوتي ! الرب رجائي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r3.claim: The psalm says God rescues the speaker from violent waters and stronger enemies, supports him, and brings him into spaciousness because He takes delight in him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r3.anchor: أرسل من العلى وأخذني , نشلني من المياه الغزيرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r4.claim: God repays the speaker according to his righteousness and clean hands; He is faithful to the pure and upright, acts against the crooked, saves the humble, and humbles the proud.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r4.anchor: جازاني الرب مثل بري , ومثل طهر يدي يعطيني

BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r5.claim: God lights the speaker's lamp, enables escape from ambush and passage over walls, and is perfect in His way; His tested word saves all who trust Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r5.anchor: وأنت يا رب تضيء سراجي , لأني بك أنجو من الرصد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r6.claim: God equips the speaker for battle, strengthens and raises him, gives victory over attackers, and leaves enemies unable to stand or obtain a rescuer.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r6.anchor: علم يدي القتال , شدد ذراعي مثل قوس نحاس , أعطاني الخلاص

BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r7.claim: The speaker asks rescue from hostile speech, becomes chief over peoples, and sees foreigners serve him; he praises God for deliverance and vengeance over his enemies.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p119/r7.anchor: نجني من مقاومة الألسن , سيرني راسا على الشعوب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r1.claim: The cited Psalm depicts a persecuted speaker grounding trust in God in the deliverance of the ancestors who trusted Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r1.anchor: بك آمن آباؤنا , وتوكلوا عليك فنجيتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r2.claim: The speaker describes mockery, assault, pierced hands and feet, and enemies dividing his clothing.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r2.anchor: ثقبوا يدي ورجلي , وزعزعوا جميع عظامي , نظروا إلي وشمتوني

BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r3.claim: After rescue, the speaker praises God; the poor are satisfied, peoples and kings worship, and later generations proclaim God's justice.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r3.anchor: يأكل المساكين ويشبعون , ويسجد قدامه جميع قبائل الشعوب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r4.claim: The following Psalm contrasts trust in God with delight in false idols and pleads for rescue from distress and enemies.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p121/r4.anchor: شنأت الذين يغتبطون بالأوثان الباطله , وأنا على الرب توكلت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r1.claim: The Psalm says God shelters those who trust Him, hears their cries, rebukes the proud, and calls the faithful to courage.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r1.anchor: ما أكثر رحمتك يارب لجميع خائفيك , أعددتها لمن اعتصم بك أمام بني البشر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r2.claim: The next Psalm calls people to praise and fear God, promising goodness to those who seek and trust Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r2.anchor: ذقوا وتيقنوا طيب الرب , طوبى للرجل المتوكل عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r3.claim: It instructs hearers to avoid deceit and evil and pursue good and peace; God watches the righteous and opposes evildoers.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r3.anchor: اكفف لسانك من الشر وشفتيك , لا تتكلم بالغدر , ابعد عن الشر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r4.claim: The Psalm says God rescues the righteous from adversity, preserves their bones, and brings the wicked to ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p122/r4.anchor: الأبرار دعوا فاستجاب لهم الرب , من جميع شدائدهم نجاهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r1.claim: The Psalmist asks God to judge his persecutors, describing false witnesses who accuse him over matters he did not know.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r1.anchor: قام علي شهود الزور , وعما لم أعلم سألوني

BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r2.claim: He says he mourned and fasted for those who harmed him, yet they gathered to mock and gloat over him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r2.anchor: عندما لجوا علي لبست مسحا , وبالصيام أذللت نفسي , وصلاتي عادت إلى حضني

BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r3.claim: He asks for deliverance and vindication, then vows to praise God among the congregation as the righteous rejoice.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r3.anchor: لأشكرك يا رب في الجمع الكثيرة وفي الشعب الصالح أرتل لك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r4.claim: The final Psalm says the wicked wither, while the meek inherit the earth and the Lord preserves the righteous until the wicked perish.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p123/r4.anchor: أهل الدعة يرثون الأرض , ويتنعمون بكثرة السلامة

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-dhikr as the Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} القرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the earth inherited by the righteous is the Garden.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون} قال: أرض الجنة

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the Qur'an was written after the Torah and that the earth in the promise is Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} قال: يعني بالذكر كتبنا في القرآن من بعد التوراة

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies al-dhikr as the Torah and al-zabur as the books revealed after it.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} يعني بالذكر التوراة ويعني بالزبور الكتب من بعد التوراة

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r5.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas says al-zabur means the books and al-dhikr means the Torah.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور} قال: الكتب {من بعد الذكر} قال: التوراة

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the Zabur as the Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: الزبور التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas calls al-dhikr the heavenly original from which the revealed books were copied.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: الزبور التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن والذكر الأصل الذي نسخت منه هذه الكتب الذي في السماء

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r8.claim: In the same report, Ibn Abbas identifies the promised earth as Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: الزبور التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن والذكر الأصل الذي نسخت منه هذه الكتب الذي في السماء والأرض أرض الجنة

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r9.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies al-zabur as the Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور} قال: الزبور التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r10.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies al-dhikr as the record in heaven.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور} قال: الزبور التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن {من بعد الذكر} قال: الذكر الذي في السماء

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r11.claim: Mujahid says al-zabur means the books, al-dhikr is the Umm al-Kitab with God, and the earth is Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال: الزبور الكتب والذكر أم الكتاب عند الله والأرض الجنة

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says al-zabur means the books revealed to the prophets and al-dhikr is the Umm al-Kitab where things were recorded beforehand.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r12.anchor: عن ابن زيد في الآية قال: الزبور الكتب التي أنزلت على الأنبياء والذكر أم الكتاب الذي يكتب فيه الأشياء قبل ذلك

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Torah, Zabur, and God's prior knowledge promised that Muhammad's community would inherit the earth and enter Paradise as the righteous.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور} الآية قال: أخبر الله سبحانه في التوراة والزبور وسابق علمه

DURR-FULL:v5p684/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas says Paradise is inherited by those who perform the five daily prayers in congregation.
DURR-FULL:v5p684/r15.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون} قال: أرض الجنة يرثها الذين

DURR-FULL:v5p686/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r1.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r1.claim: Al-Sha'bi says this is in David's Zabur after the mention of Moses' Torah, and that the earth is Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r1.anchor: عن الشعبي في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} قال: في زبور داود {من بعد} ذكر موسى

DURR-FULL:v5p686/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r2.claim: Ikrima gives the same interpretation: David's Zabur follows the mention of Moses' Torah.
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r2.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم عن عكرمة مثله

DURR-FULL:v5p686/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r3.claim: Qatada says God wrote this in David's Zabur after the Torah.
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: كتب الله في زبور داود بعد التوراة

DURR-FULL:v5p686/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the promised earth is Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله: {أن الأرض يرثها} قال: الجنة

DURR-FULL:v5p686/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says Paradise begins in the earth and rises through levels, while Hell begins in the earth and descends; a barrier lies between them, with Paradise ascending into heaven and Hell descending into earth.
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله: {أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون} قال: الجنة وقرأ

DURR-FULL:v5p686/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r6.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله أبو اليمان
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r6.claim: Abu al-Yaman says the earth is a gathering place for believers' souls until the resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r6.anchor: عن صفوان قال: سألت عامر بن عبد الله أبا اليمان هل لأنفس المؤمنين مجتمع فقال:

DURR-FULL:v5p686/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda transmits a divine statement about the earth passing to God's righteous servants, followed by the Prophet's identification of his community as the righteous.
DURR-FULL:v5p686/r7.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال الله تعالى: {أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون} فنحن الصالحون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r1.claim: If earth means Paradise, the verse follows naturally after the preceding passage about Paradise and also connects with the promise of the earth's diminishing from its edges.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r1.anchor: إن كان المراد بالأرض أرض الجنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r2.claim: If it means worldly land, the promise comforts believers harmed in Mecca and its vicinity: their condition will improve in this life as well as in the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r2.anchor: أي مصيرها بيد عباد الله الصالحين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r3.claim: The broad expression earth can also promise worldly dominion to Muslims as long as they remain faithful and righteous; God fulfilled the promise in both worldly and afterlife senses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r3.anchor: على أن في إطلاق اسم الأرض ما يصلح لإرادة أن سلطان العالم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r4.speaker: ثوبان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r4.claim: Thawban reports the Prophet saying God folded the earth for him, showed him its eastern and western reaches, and his community's rule would extend as far as he had seen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r4.anchor: عن ثوبان قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r5.claim: The majority read Zabur in the singular, a passive participle meaning something written, on the pattern of words for a milch or rideable camel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { في الزبور } بصيغة الإفراد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r6.speaker: حمزة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r6.claim: Hamza reads the plural Zubur, from singular zubr meaning a written book, on the pattern of qishr and qushur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بصيغة الجمع { زبور بوزن فعول جمع زبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r7.claim: On the majority's singular reading, Zabur usually names David's book; the specific promise is notable because earlier scriptures had no general promise that the righteous would inherit the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p161/r7.anchor: فعلى قراءة الجمهور فو غالب في الإطلاق على كتاب داوود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r1.claim: The Zabur is David's book, preserved in the Jewish Psalms; Ibn Ashur says he cannot now identify the Psalm containing this promise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r1.anchor: والزبور : كتاب داوود وهو مبثوث في الكتاب المسمى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r2.speaker: فويدو
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r2.claim: The Italian Arabist Foido cited a Hebrew wording meaning the righteous inherit the earth as testimony that this promise existed in earlier scripture before its Qur'anic formulation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r2.anchor: ووجدت في محاضرة للإيطالي المستعرب ( فويدو )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r3.claim: On Hamza's plural reading, the promise was repeated across scriptures for different communities of righteous servants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r3.anchor: وعلى قراءة حمزة أن هذا الوعد تكرر في الكتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r4.claim: After the reminder can mean after admonition and instruction to the community: after commands, they were promised inheritance of the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r4.anchor: ومعنى { من بعد الذكر } أن ذلك الوعد ورد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r5.claim: Another view takes the reminder as the Torah, the law-book given to Moses, which the Qur'an calls guidance and reminder for the God-fearing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد ب { الذكر } كتاب الشريعة وهو التوراة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r6.claim: On the Torah reading, the prepositional phrase is a settled circumstantial qualifier of Zabur, distinguishing this later promise from the earlier promise to Israel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r6.anchor: فيكون الظرف في قوله تعالى : { من بعد الذكر }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r7.claim: The later promise differs from Moses' promise of the Holy Land and Israel's earlier inheritance of political power, which preceded David and was exemplified by David's kingship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r7.anchor: وهو الوعد الذي ذكر في قوله تعالى حكاية عن موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur identifies the later righteous community as Muslims: God fulfilled the promise through the Prophet and Companions, whose rule expanded as the Prophet had foretold.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p162/r8.anchor: بل المراد الإيماء إلى أنه وعد وعده الله قوما صالحين

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r1.claim: The passage evokes a soul moving from spiritual qualities toward lordship, returning to its Lord under an eternal promise fulfilled forever.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r1.anchor: ومن وصف الروحانية إلى وصف الربوبية بجذوة ارجعي إلى ربك وعدا علينا في الأزل

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r2.claim: The Zabur is the scripture given to David, as stated in 4:163.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r2.anchor: وهو كتاب داود عليه السلام كما قال :

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r3.claim: After the Reminder means after the Torah; every heavenly book is called a reminder.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r3.anchor: بعدما كتبنا في التوراة لأن كل كتاب سماوي ذكر

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r4.claim: Zabara means writing in bold strokes; any heavily written book is a zabur, though the term is especially used for David's revealed book.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r4.anchor: قال الراغب زبرت الكتاب كتبته كتابة غليظة وكل كتاب غليظ الكتابة

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r5.claim: Another view takes zabur to mean any divine book that is difficult to comprehend.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r5.anchor: بل الزبور كل كتاب يصعب الوقوف عليه من الكتب الإلهية

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r6.claim: A further view distinguishes the Zabur, limited to rational wisdom without legal rulings, from a book containing both rulings and wisdom; David's Zabur lacks rulings.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم اسم للكتاب المقصور على الحكمة العقلية دون الأحكام الشرعية

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r7.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r7.claim: Al-Qamus defines zabur as a written book, gives zubur as its plural, and identifies it as David's book.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r7.anchor: الزبور الكتاب بمعنى المزبور والجمع زبر وكتاب داود

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r8.claim: The righteous servants generally inherit the land after disbelievers are expelled; this promises the establishment of religion and honor for its adherents, as in 24:55.

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the inherited earth is Paradise, supported by the verse describing believers inheriting a place in Paradise.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r9.anchor: أن المراد أرض الجنة كما ينبىء عنه قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r10.speaker: عرائس البقلي
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r10.claim: In primordial knowledge, Paradise's lands are inherited by the righteous for their rewards and ranks, while witnessing eternal divine majesty is the inheritance of knowers and lovers; the former behold servanthood, the latter lordship.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r10.anchor: قال في "عرائس البقلي" : كان في علم الأزلية أن أرض الجنان ميراث عباده الصالحين

BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r11.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r11.claim: Sahl says God claims them as His own and calls them righteous because their inner selves are sincerely His alone, rectified and wholly detached from all besides Him.
BURSEVI:v5p402#3/r11.anchor: قال سهل أضافهم إلى نفسه وحلاهم بحلية الصلاح معناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r16.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r16.claim: One view takes zabūr as a general name for all revealed books, derived from the verb for writing, and takes dhikr as the Preserved Tablet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r16.anchor: وقالت فرقة الزبور اسم يعم جميع الكتب المنزلة لأنه مأخوذ من زبرت الكتاب إذا كتبته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r17.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r17.claim: Another explanation identifies al-dhikr as the heavenly remembrance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r17.anchor: وقال بعضهم الذكر الذي في السماء، وقالت فرقة الزبور هو اسم زبور داود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r18.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r18.claim: Other views identify the Zabūr as David's book, or as books revealed after the Torah; both take al-dhikr as the Torah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r18.anchor: وقالت فرقة الزبور هو اسم زبور داود، والذكر أراد به التوراة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r19.speaker: حمزة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r19.claim: Ḥamza alone reads al-zubūr with a ḍamma on zāy.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r20.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r20.claim: One group interprets the earth as worldly lands that believers will possess.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r20.anchor: وقالت فرقة الأرض أراد بها أرض الدنيا أي كل ما يناله المؤمنون من الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r21.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r21.claim: Another group takes the earth as Paradise, citing 39:74, where the saved say they inherited the land and settle wherever they wish.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r21.anchor: وقالت فرقة أراد أرض الجنة، واستشهدت بقوله تعالى وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده وأورثنا الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r22.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r22.claim: A group reads this as reassurance to the audience: just as God fulfilled His promise to the Israelites, He will fulfill the promise of victory to you.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p102#2/r22.anchor: وقالت فرقة إنما أراد بهذه الآية الإخبار عما كان صنعه مع بني إسرائيل أي فاعلموا أنا كما وفينا لهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r1.claim: One view takes the Zabur as all revealed books and the dhikr as the heavenly Mother Book; it is attributed to one report from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r1.anchor: أحدها أن الزبور جميع الكتب المنزلة من السماء والذكر أم الكتاب الذي عند الله قاله سعيد بن جبير في رواية ومجاهد وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r2.claim: Ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn Abbas that the Zabur comprises the Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an, while the dhikr is what is in heaven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r2.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية ابن جبير فانه قال الزبور التوارة والإنجيل والقرآن والذكر الذي في السماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r3.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits a second view from Ibn Abbas: the Zabur means books generally, and the dhikr is the Torah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r3.anchor: والثاني أن الزبور الكتب والذكر التوراة رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r4.claim: In another report, Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the Zabur is the Qur'an and the dhikr is the Torah and Gospel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r4.anchor: والثالث أن الزبور القرآن والذكر التوراة والإنجيل قاله سعيد بن جبير في رواية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r5.speaker: الشعبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbi identifies the Zabur as David's Zabur and the dhikr as the remembrance of Moses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r5.anchor: والرابع أن الزبور زبور داود والذكر ذكر موسى ة قاله الشعبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r6.claim: One view identifies the inherited earth as the land of Paradise; Saʿid ibn Jubayr transmits it from Ibn Abbas, and most interpreters agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r6.anchor: أحدها أنه أرض الجنة رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس وبه قال الاكثرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r7.claim: A second view, also transmitted from Ibn Abbas, identifies the earth as the earthly world.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r7.anchor: والثاني أرض الدنيا وهو منقول عن ابن عباس أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r8.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r8.claim: Ibn al-Saib identifies the earth as the Holy Land.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r8.anchor: والثالث الأرض المقدسة قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r9.claim: One view says the righteous servants are Muhammad's community; Ibn Abi Talha transmits from Ibn Abbas that they inherit the earthly lands through conquests.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r9.anchor: أحدها أنهم أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس وفي رواية ترث أمه محمد أرض الدنيا بالفتوح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r10.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r10.claim: Ibn al-Saib says the righteous servants are the Children of Israel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r10.anchor: والثاني بنو اسرائيل قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r11.speaker: بعض فقهاء المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r11.claim: Some jurist-interpreters take the phrase generally to mean every righteous person.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p397/r11.anchor: والثالث أنه عام في كل صالح قاله بعض فقهاء المفسرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r1.claim: God decreed happiness in both lives and the righteous inheriting the earth; this is written in scriptural and predestined books and must occur.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى مخبرا عما حتمه وقضاه لعباده الصالحين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r2.claim: Al-A'mash reports Sa'id ibn Jubayr interpreting al-Zabur collectively as the Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r2.anchor: قال الأعمش: سألت سعيد بن جبير عن قوله تعالى: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r3.claim: Mujahid explains al-Zabur simply as the scripture or book.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، الشعبي، الحسن، قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Qatada, and others identify al-Zabur as the revelation to David and al-dhikr as the Torah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والشعبي، والحسن، وقتادة، وغير واحد: الزبور: الذي أنزل على داود، والذكر: التوراة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r5.claim: A separate report from Ibn Abbas identifies al-Zabur as the Qur'an.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says al-dhikr is that which is in heaven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: الذكر: الذي في السماء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r7.claim: Mujahid says al-Zabur means books subsequent to al-dhikr and al-dhikr is God's Mother of the Book; Ibn Jarir chooses this interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الزبور: الكتب بعد الذكر، والذكر: أم الكتاب عند الله. واختار ذلك ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies al-dhikr as the original first book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r8.anchor: وكذا قال زيد بن أسلم: هو الكتاب الأول.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r9.speaker: الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r9.claim: Al-Thawri identifies al-dhikr as the Preserved Tablet.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r10.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r10.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam says al-Zabur is the books revealed to prophets and al-dhikr is the Mother of the Book in which prior decrees are recorded.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r10.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: الزبور: الكتب التي نزلت على الأنبياء، والذكر: أم الكتاب الذي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, says the Torah, Zabur, and God's prior knowledge promised that Muhammad's righteous community would inherit the earth and enter Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r11.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: أخبر الله سبحانه (3) في التوراة والزبور وسابق علمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Mujahid, and a group of early authorities interpret the earth inherited by the righteous as the land of Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p384/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد، عن ابن عباس: {أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون} قال: أرض الجنة.

JISHUMI:v7p4894/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4894/r10.speaker: حمزة
JISHUMI:v7p4894/r10.claim: Ḥamza reads الزبور with a damma on zāy; the others use a fatha, and both are dialect forms.
JISHUMI:v7p4894/r10.anchor: وقرأ حمزة: الزبور بضم الزاي، والباقون بفتحها، وهما لغتان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r1.speaker: الشعبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbī identifies al-Zabūr as David’s Psalms and al-dhikr as the Torah.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r1.anchor: عن الشعبي رحمة الله عليه : زبور داود عليه السلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r2.claim: Al-dhikr may mean the scriptures generally or the Mother Book, the Preserved Tablet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r2.anchor: وقيل اسم لجنس ما أنزل على الأنبياء من الكتب . والذكر : أم الكتاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r3.claim: One view says believers inherit earth after unbelievers are expelled, as in 7:137 and Moses’ statement in 7:128.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r3.anchor: أي : يرثها المؤمنون بعد إجلاء الكفار ، كقوله تعالى : { وأورثنا القوم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the earth is Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : هي أرض الجنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r5.claim: Another view says the Holy Land will be inherited by Muḥammad’s community.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p139/r5.anchor: وقيل : الأرض المقدسة ، ترثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUJAHID:v1p417#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p417#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p417#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the Reminder as the Mother of the Book held with God.
MUJAHID:v1p417#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد الذكر أم الكتاب عند الله

MUJAHID:v1p417#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p417#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p417#2/r2.claim: The earth that the righteous inherit is the land of Paradise.
MUJAHID:v1p417#2/r2.anchor: والأرض أرض الجنة ﴿ يرثها عبادي الصالحون ﴾

MUQATIL:21:104-106/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:104-106/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:104-106/r4.claim: Muqatil identifies the scriptures called Zabur here as the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms; al-dhikr is the Preserved Tablet.
MUQATIL:21:104-106/r4.anchor: { ولقد كتبنا في الزبور } يعنى التوراة والإنجيل والزبور { من بعد الذكر } يعنى اللوح المحفوظ

MUQATIL:21:104-106/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:104-106/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:104-106/r5.claim: The earth belongs to God and His righteous servants who inherit it are the believers.
MUQATIL:21:104-106/r5.anchor: لله { يرثها عبادي الصالحون } [آية: 105] يعنى المؤمنون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r1.claim: The Zabur is the Book given to David.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r2.claim: On the first reading, “the Reminder” is the Torah.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r3.claim: On the first interpretation, the land is Syria, and its heirs are Muhammad’s community.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r3.anchor: ﴿ إن الأرض ﴾ أي الشام ﴿ يرثها عبادي ﴾ ساكنة الياء حمزة غيره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r4.claim: Hamza reads the final yāʾ in “My servants” as still; other readers give it fatḥa.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r4.anchor: ساكنة الياء حمزة غيره بفتح الياء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r5.claim: Alternatively, Zabur means written scripture generally, while “the Reminder” is the Preserved Tablet from which all scriptures derive.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r5.anchor: أو الزبور بمعنى المزبور أي المكتوب يعني ما أنزال على الأنبياء من الكتب والذكر أم الكتاب يعني اللوح

NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r6.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r6.claim: Hamza and Khalaf read the plural zubur, meaning written scriptures.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r6.anchor: قراءة حمزة وخلف بضم الزاي على جمع الزبر بمعنى المزبور

NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p93/r7.claim: On the alternative interpretation, the land is the Garden.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r1.claim: Zabur and book are equivalent terms: zabara means “to write,” and zubur is its plural, so the Torah and Gospel may also be called zabur.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r1.anchor: الزبور والكتاب واحد ولذلك جاز أن يقال للتوراة والإنجيل زبور

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the Zabur means the Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an, while the Reminder is the heavenly record.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: «الزبور» التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r3.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r3.claim: Al-Sha'bi identifies the Zabur as David's Psalms and the Reminder as Moses' Torah.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r3.anchor: الشعبي: «الزبور» زبور داود، و«الذكر» توراة موسى عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r4.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r4.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd say the Zabur means the prophets' books and the Reminder is the heavenly Mother of the Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r4.anchor: مجاهد وابن زيد: «الزبور» كتب الأنبياء عليهم السلام، و«الذكر» أم الكتاب الذي عند الله في السماء

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Zabur means books sent to prophets after Moses and the Reminder is the Torah revealed to Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «الزبور» الكتب التي أنزلها الله من بعد موسى على أنبيائه

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r6.speaker: حمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r6.claim: Hamza reads الزُّبُر with a ḍamma on zāy, using the plural form zubur.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «في الزبور» بضم الزاي جمع زبر

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r7.claim: The best interpretation is that “the earth” is the earth of Paradise: worldly land has already been inherited by righteous and unrighteous alike; this is also attributed to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r7.anchor: أحسن ما قيل فيه أنه يراد بها أرض الجنة كما قال سعيد بن جبير لأن الأرض في الدنيا قد ورثها الصالحون وغيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r8.speaker: مجاهد وأبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r8.claim: Mujahid and Abu al-Aliya cite the people of Paradise saying God fulfilled His promise and gave them the earth as evidence for the Paradise interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد وأبو العالية: ودليل هذا التأويل قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the inherited land as the Holy Land.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أنها الأرض المقدسة

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r10.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says Muhammad's community inherits the lands of unbelieving nations through conquest.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r10.anchor: وعنه أيضا: أنها أرض الأمم الكافرة ترثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالفتوح

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r11.speaker: قيل
