QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r11.claim: Another view identifies the righteous inheritors as the Children of Israel, citing their inheritance of the blessed land.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r11.anchor: وقيل: إن المراد بذلك بنو إسرائيل بدليل قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r12.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r12.claim: Most commentators identify the righteous servants as Muhammad's community.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r12.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن المراد بالعباد الصالحين أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r13.speaker: حمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:21:105-106/r13.claim: Hamza reads the yāʾ in عبادي as quiescent.

QASHANI:21:104-105/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:104-105/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:104-105/r5.claim: One reading is that the heart's Psalter records, after the Preserved Tablet, the body's earth being inherited by righteous, illuminated faculties once vicious powers are destroyed by discipline.
QASHANI:21:104-105/r5.anchor: زبور القلب { من بعد الذكر } في اللوح أن أرض البدن يرثها القوى الصالحة المنورة

QASHANI:21:104-105/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:104-105/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:104-105/r6.claim: Alternatively, the Preserved Tablet after the Mother Book records the earth inherited by spirit, secret, heart, intellect, soul, and all faculties through uprightness after their annihilation in unity.
QASHANI:21:104-105/r6.anchor: أو: ولقد كتبنا في زبور اللوح المحفوظ من بعد الذكر في أم الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v22p198/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198/r8.speaker: حمزة والباقون
RAZI-FULL:v22p198/r8.claim: Hamza reads “al-zubur” with a damma on zāy; the other readers use a fatha. Both readings mean the book.
RAZI-FULL:v22p198/r8.anchor: قرأ حمزة بضم الزاي والباقون بفتحها يعني الزبور

RAZI-FULL:v22p198/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p198/r9.claim: The root zabara means to write; “mazbūr” is the plural of zubr, and al-zabūr is a book, like the forms “al-halūb” and “al-rakūb.”
RAZI-FULL:v22p198/r9.anchor: يقال : زبرت الكتاب أي كتبته والمزبور بضم الزاي جمع زبر كقشر وقشور

RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد والكلبي ومقاتل وابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r1.claim: These authorities take the “Zubur” as revealed books and the “Remembrance” as the heavenly Mother Book, where future events are written for the angels and from which prophetic books are copied.
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r1.anchor: وهو قول سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد والكلبي ومقاتل وابن زيد الزبور هو الكتب المنزلة

RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r2.speaker: قتادة والشعبي
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r2.claim: Qatada and al-Shaʿbi identify the Zubur as the Qur’an and the Remembrance as the Torah.
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r2.anchor: وثانيها : الزبور هو القرآن والذكر هو التوراة وهو قول قتادة والشعبي

RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r3.claim: A third view makes the Zubur David’s Psalter and the Remembrance something reported from David: “God existed and nothing was with Him, then He created the Remembrance.”
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r3.anchor: وثالثها : الزبور زبور داود عليه السلام ، والذكر هو الذي يروى عنه عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi’s own fourth view takes “the Remembrance” to mean God’s knowledge: God wrote this in the Zubur after already knowing it without forgetfulness, so His promise must occur.
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r4.anchor: وعندي فيه وجه رابع : وهو أن المراد بالذكر العلم أي كتبنا ذلك في الزبور

RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة والسدي وأبو العالية
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r5.claim: These authorities take the earth as Paradise and the righteous servants as believers who obey God: God recorded that the righteous will inherit Paradise, citing the blessed inheritance of the Garden and the post-resurrection context.
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r5.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة والسدي وأبي العالية

RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة والسدي وأبو العالية
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r6.claim: Their argument is that Paradise is specially intended for the righteous, while the unrighteous have a place there only as dependents; worldly earth is shared by righteous and unrighteous, and the verse follows resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r6.anchor: وأما ثانيا : فلأنها الأرض التي يختص بها الصالحون لأنها لهم خلقت ، وغيرهم إذا حصل

RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r7.claim: An unattributed report describes Paradise’s earth as white and pure in support of interpreting “earth” as the Garden.
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r7.anchor: فقد روى في الخبر أنها أرض الجنة فإنها بيضاء نقية

RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي وابن عباس في بعض الروايات
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi and some reports from Ibn Abbas take the earth as the worldly earth, which God will make believers inherit; they cite the promise of succession and Moses’ statement that God gives the earth to whichever servants He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r8.anchor: وهو قول الكلبي وابن عباس في بعض الروايات ودليل هذا القول قوله سبحانه : { وعد الله

RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r9.claim: A third view identifies the earth as the Holy Land, citing the inheritance of the lands blessed around it; ultimately Muhammad’s community inherits it when Jesus son of Mary descends.
RAZI-FULL:v22p198#2/r9.anchor: وثالثها : هي الأرض المقدسة يرثها الصالحون ، ودليله قوله تعالى ؛ { وأورثنا القوم

QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r19.claim: Here al-dhikr refers to the Torah.

QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r20.claim: Here katabnā means that God announced and decreed the matter.

QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r21.claim: The righteous servants who inherit the earth are Muhammad's community.
QUSHAYRI:v2p306/r21.anchor: و { الصالحون } أمة محمد - - أن { الأرض } هم الذين يرثونها

STUDYQURAN:21:105/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r1.claim: The Psalms are also mentioned in 4:163 and 17:55.

STUDYQURAN:21:105/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r2.claim: Zabūr is often treated as synonymous with kitāb, meaning “book” or “scripture.”
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r2.anchor: often considered a synonym for kitāb

STUDYQURAN:21:105/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r3.speaker: R and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r3.claim: Some interpret Zabūr as all the prophets’ books, including the Torah, Gospel, and Quran, rather than only David’s Psalms.
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r3.anchor: prophets (R, Ṭ), which would include the Torah, the Gospel, and the Quran (Q,Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:21:105/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r4.speaker: R and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r4.claim: The Reminder is interpreted as what is in Heaven, the Mother of the Book with God.
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r4.anchor: The Reminder is what is in Heaven (Ṭ), the Mother of the Book (3:7; 13:39; 43:4), with God (R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:21:105/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r5.speaker: Q and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r5.claim: Some commentators take the earth to be the earth of the Garden, a celestial earth belonging to believers rather than the shared earthly world.
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r5.anchor: Some commentators the earth refers to “the earth of the Garden” (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:21:105/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r6.speaker: R and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r6.claim: Others understand the earth as this world, specifically disbelievers’ lands that Muhammad’s community will inherit.
STUDYQURAN:21:105/r6.anchor: others say that the earth refers to this world (R, Ṭ) and denotes disbelievers’ lands that would be inherited by the community of Muhammad

TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r1.claim: Saʿid identifies the Dhikr as that in Heaven; the report also says the revealed books are the Zabur, Torah, Gospel, and Qurʾan.
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r1.anchor: سألت سعيدا، عن قول الله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: الذكر: الذي في السماء

TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r2.speaker: الأعمش
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads الزبر rather than الزبور and associates the wording with the Zabur, Torah, Gospel, and Qurʾan.
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r2.anchor: قرأها الأعمش «الزبر» قال: " الزبور، والتوراة، والإنجيل، والقرآن {من بعد الذكر} [الأنبياء: 105]

TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r3.claim: Mujahid takes al-Zabur to mean the Book and al-Dhikr to mean the Mother of the Book with God.
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: {الزبور} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: " الكتاب. {من بعد الذكر} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: أم الكتاب عند الله "

TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says al-Zabur means the books sent to the prophets, while al-Dhikr is the Mother of the Book where matters were recorded beforehand.
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: " الزبور: الكتب التي أنزلت على الأنبياء. والذكر: أم الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r5.claim: Saʿid says the writing was in the Qurʾan after the Torah.
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r5.anchor: عن سعيد، في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: «كتبنا في القرآن من بعد التوراة»

TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies al-Dhikr as the Torah and al-Zabur as the books revealed to prophets after Moses.
TAB-FULL:v16p431#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} [الأنبياء: 105] الآية، قال: " الذكر: التوراة، والزبور: الكتب "

TAB-FULL:v16p433/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says al-Dhikr is the Torah and al-Zabur after the Torah means the other revealed books.
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r1.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول، في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} [الأنبياء: 105] الآية , قال: " الذكر: التوراة، ويعني بالزبور من بعد التوراة: الكتب "

TAB-FULL:v16p433/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r2.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r2.claim: ʿAmir says al-Zabur is David's Zabur, and al-Dhikr is the Torah, the remembrance of Moses.
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r2.anchor: عن عامر، أنه قال في هذه الآية: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: " زبور داود من بعد الذكر: ذكر موسى: التوراة "

TAB-FULL:v16p433/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r3.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi likewise identifies al-Zabur as David's Psalm and al-Dhikr as the remembrance of Moses.
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي أنه قال في هذه الآية: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: " في زبور داود، من بعد ذكر موسى

TAB-FULL:v16p433/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Saʿid and Mujahid: the verse records in revealed books what God had already written in the Mother of the Book; zabara means to write, every revealed book is Dhikr, and the definite article signals a known record, unlike the Torah or earlier Abrahamic scrolls.
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r4.anchor: وأن كل كتاب أنزله الله إلى نبي من أنبيائه، فهو ذكر. فإذ كان ذلك كذلك، فإن في إدخاله الألف واللام في الذكر، الدلالة البينة

TAB-FULL:v16p433/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Mujahid, identifies the earth inherited by the righteous as the Garden's earth.
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {أن الأرض، يرثها عبادي الصالحون} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: «أرض الجنة»

TAB-FULL:v16p433/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r6.claim: Al-Tabari interprets the inherited earth as the Garden, bestowed on servants who obey God and His commands and prohibitions rather than disobeying Him and preferring Satan.
TAB-FULL:v16p433/r6.anchor: يعني بذلك: أن أرض الجنة يرثها عبادي، العاملون بطاعته، المنتهون إلى أمره ونهيه من عباده،

TAB-FULL:v16p436/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God had decreed in the Torah, Zabur, and prior knowledge that Muhammad's community would inherit the earth and enter the Garden as the righteous.
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: «أخبر سبحانه في التوراة والزبور وسابق علمه

TAB-FULL:v16p436/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r2.claim: Saʿid says the writing was in the Qurʾan after the Torah and that the earth is the Garden.
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: " كتبنا في القرآن بعد التوراة، والأرض: أرض الجنة "

TAB-FULL:v16p436/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r3.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says the earth inherited by the righteous is the Garden.
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية: {أن الأرض، يرثها عبادي الصالحون} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: " الأرض: الجنة "

TAB-FULL:v16p436/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r4.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r4.claim: Saʿid, when asked by al-Aʿmash, identifies the earth as the Garden.
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r4.anchor: سألت سعيدا عن قول الله: {أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: «أرض الجنة»

TAB-FULL:v16p436/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r5.claim: Mujahid also says the earth means the Garden.
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {أن الأرض} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: " الجنة، {يرثها عبادي الصالحون} [الأنبياء: 105] "

TAB-FULL:v16p436/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the earth as the Garden and cites 39:74, where its inhabitants say God fulfilled His promise and made them inherit the land.
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون} [الأنبياء: 105] قال: " الجنة. وقرأ قول الله جل ثناؤه:

TAB-FULL:v16p436/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Garden rises through the heavens while Hell descends into the earth, separated by a wall; he cites 57:13 about its inner mercy and outer punishment.
TAB-FULL:v16p436/r7.anchor: قال: فالجنة مبتدؤها في الأرض , ثم تذهب درجات علوا، والنار مبتدؤها في الأرض، وبينهما حجاب سور، ما يدري أحد ما ذاك السور،

TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r1.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله أبو اليمان
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r1.claim: Abu al-Yaman says the verse's earth is where believers' spirits gather until resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r1.anchor: سألت عامر بن عبد الله أبا اليمان: هل لأنفس المؤمنين مجتمع؟ قال: فقال: " إن الأرض التي يقول الله

TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r2.claim: Another reported view takes the earth as the worldly land God grants to believers.
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي الأرض يورثها الله المؤمنين في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r3.claim: Another view says the verse concerns the Children of Israel, whom God promised this inheritance and for whom He fulfilled it, citing 7:137.
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: عني بذلك بنو إسرائيل، وذلك أن الله وعدهم ذلك، فوفى لهم به.

TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r4.claim: A view attributed to Ibn Abbas through ʿAli ibn Abi Talha says Muhammad's community inherits the lands of unbelieving peoples.
TAB-FULL:v16p436#2/r4.anchor: أنها أرض الأمم الكافرة، ترثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. وهو قول ابن عباس

SULAMI:v2p17#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p17#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p17#2/r1.claim: God calls them His own and adorns them with righteousness: those fit for Him are wholly sincere, have mended their inner selves, and cut themselves off from everything besides Him.
SULAMI:v2p17#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل : أضافهم إلى نفسه وحلاهم بحلية الصلاح

TAB-FULL:v1p96/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r1.claim: In the cited Arabic verse fragment, kitab means “written.”
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r1.anchor: كتاب مثل ما لصق الغراء. يعني به مكتوبا

TAB-FULL:v1p96/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r2.claim: Dhikr may mean a reminder from God that teaches servants His limits, duties, and wisdom, or honor and renown for believers.
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r2.anchor: وأما تأويل اسمه الذي هو الذكر، فإنه محتمل معنيين: أحدهما أنه ذكر من الله جل ذكره

TAB-FULL:v1p96/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r4.claim: Tabari says the names of Quran suras were given by the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r4.anchor: ثم لسور القرآن أسماء سماها بها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v1p96/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r5.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r5.claim: Wathila ibn al-Asqa' reports the Prophet's mapping: the seven long suras replace the Torah, the mi'un the Psalms, the mathani the Gospel, and the Mufassal is an added distinction.
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r5.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «أعطيت مكان التوراة السبع الطول، وأعطيت مكان الزبور المئين، وأعطيت مكان الإنجيل المثاني، وفضلت بالمفصل»

TAB-FULL:v1p96/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r6.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r6.claim: Abu Qilaba reports the Prophet mapping the seven long suras to the Torah, mathani to the Psalms, mi'un to the Gospel, and Mufassal as a special favor.
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r6.anchor: عن أبي قلابة، قال: قال رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v1p96/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r7.speaker: خالد
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r7.claim: Khalid says people called the Mufassal “the Arabic”; some said there is no prostration in the Arabic (Mufassal).
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r7.anchor: قال خالد: كانوا يسمون المفصل: العربي؛ قال خالد: قال بعضهم

TAB-FULL:v1p96/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r8.claim: Ibn Mas'ud compares the long suras to the Torah, the mi'un to the Gospel, the mathani to the Psalms, and says the remainder exceeds the other books.

TAB-FULL:v1p96/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r9.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r9.claim: Another report from Wathila says God gave the Prophet the seven long suras for the Torah, mathani for the Gospel, mi'un for the Psalms, and favored him with Mufassal.
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r9.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «أعطاني ربي مكان التوراة السبع الطول، ومكان الإنجيل المثاني، ومكان الزبور المئين، وفضلني بالمفصل»

TUSTARI:21:105/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:21:105/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:21:105/r1.claim: God calls the inheritors His servants and marks them as righteous: only those wholly sincere for Him, who have made their inner life sound and cut themselves off from all besides Him, are fit for this inheritance.
TUSTARI:21:105/r1.anchor: أضافهم إلى نفسه وحلاهم بحلية الصلاح

TABATABAI:21:105/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r1.claim: Al-Zabur most likely means David’s scripture, which God names as a Zabur elsewhere; proposals that it means the Qur’an or revealed books generally, including those after Moses, lack evidence.
TABATABAI:21:105/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالزبور كتاب داود عليه السلام وقد سمي بهذا الاسم في قوله وآتينا داود زبورا

TABATABAI:21:105/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:21:105/r2.claim: An alternative says al-Zabur means the Qur’an or all revealed books, or books revealed to prophets after Moses; the author finds no evidence for these readings.

TABATABAI:21:105/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:21:105/r3.claim: One view identifies the dhikr as the Torah, which this sura calls ‘reminder’ in two places.
TABATABAI:21:105/r3.anchor: والمراد بالذكر قيل هو التوراة وقد سماها الله به في موضعين من هذه السورة

TABATABAI:21:105/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:21:105/r4.claim: Another view takes dhikr as the Qur’an, which God calls a reminder in several passages; on this reading, ‘after’ marks rank rather than chronology.
TABATABAI:21:105/r4.anchor: وقيل هو القرآن وقد سماه الله ذكرا في مواضع من كلامه وكون الزبور بعد الذكر على هذا القول بعدية رتبية

TABATABAI:21:105/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:21:105/r5.claim: A further view identifies dhikr as the Preserved Tablet; the author dismisses it as untenable.
TABATABAI:21:105/r5.anchor: وقيل هو اللوح المحفوظ وهو كما ترى

TABATABAI:21:105/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r6.claim: Inheritance means property passing to someone without a transaction; here it is transfer of authority over earth’s benefits and the establishment of life’s blessings among the inheritors.
TABATABAI:21:105/r6.anchor: والمراد من وراثة الأرض انتقال التسلط على منافعها

TABATABAI:21:105/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r7.claim: Worldly inheritance means the earth is cleansed of idolatry and disobedience and inhabited by a righteous society worshiping God alone, as in the promise of succession to believers.
TABATABAI:21:105/r7.anchor: كالتمتع الصالح بأمتعتها وزيناتها فيكون مؤدى الآية أن الأرض ستتطهر من الشرك والمعصية

TABATABAI:21:105/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r8.claim: The worldly reading connects the verse’s inheritance with God’s promise that believers will succeed to the earth and worship without associating partners with Him.
TABATABAI:21:105/r8.anchor: كما يشير إليه قوله تعالى وعد الله الذين آمنوا منكم وعملوا الصالحات ليستخلفنهم في الأرض

TABATABAI:21:105/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r9.claim: Otherworldly inheritance means stations of nearness gained in earthly life, which become the bliss of the afterlife.
TABATABAI:21:105/r9.anchor: وإما أخروية وهي مقامات القرب التي اكتسبوها في حياتهم الدنيا فإنها من بركات الحياة الأرضية

TABATABAI:21:105/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r10.claim: The afterlife reading is supported by the saved people saying they inherited the earth in Paradise and by the description of believers as inheritors of Paradise.
TABATABAI:21:105/r10.anchor: كما يشير إليه قوله تعالى حكاية عن أهل الجنة وقالوا الحمد لله الذي أورثنا الأرض

TABATABAI:21:105/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r11.claim: The verse is unrestricted and includes both worldly and otherworldly inheritance; neither sense should be made exclusive.
TABATABAI:21:105/r11.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن الآية مطلقة ولا موجب لتخصيصها بإحدى الوراثتين

TABATABAI:21:105/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r12.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:21:105/r12.claim: Some restrict inheritance to the afterlife, arguing from the preceding verse’s mention of resurrection that no earth remains afterward for the righteous to inherit.
TABATABAI:21:105/r12.anchor: فهم بين من يخصها بالوراثة الأخروية

TABATABAI:21:105/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r13.claim: He rejects the afterlife-only argument: attachment to the preceding verse is not required, since this verse may attach to the earlier statement about believers who do righteous deeds.
TABATABAI:21:105/r13.anchor: فمن الممكن أن تكون معطوفة على قوله السابق

TABATABAI:21:105/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r14.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:21:105/r14.claim: Others restrict inheritance to worldly rule at the rise of Islam or the appearance of the Mahdi, citing relevant verses and widely transmitted reports through both Sunni and Shi‘i routes.
TABATABAI:21:105/r14.anchor: وبين من يخصها بالوراثة الدنيوية ويحملها على زمان ظهور الإسلام أو ظهور المهدي عليه السلام

TABATABAI:21:105/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r15.claim: The context links this verse to the earlier account of believers’ recompense: the previous passage details their afterlife reward, while this one details worldly recompense through inheriting the earth.
TABATABAI:21:105/r15.anchor: الاعتبار بالسياق أن تكون معطوفة على قوله السابق

TABATABAI:21:105/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:105/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:105/r16.claim: Humankind was commanded to one religion but split: the differing afterlife recompense favors believers, while the earthly recompense grants inheritance to the righteous rather than others.
TABATABAI:21:105/r16.anchor: أنا أمرناهم بدين واحد لكنهم تقطعوا واختلفوا فاختلف مجازاتنا لهم أما في الآخرة فللمؤمنين سعي مشكور

TABRISI:21:104-105/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-105/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، مجاهد، ابن زيد
TABRISI:21:104-105/r13.claim: They take al-Zabur as the prophets’ revealed books and al-Dhikr as the heavenly Preserved Tablet; al-Zajjaj prefers this because zabūr and kitāb both mean writing.
TABRISI:21:104-105/r13.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وابن زيد وهو اختيار الزجاج قال لأن الزبور والكتاب بمعنى واحد وزبرت كتبت

TABRISI:21:104-105/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-105/r14.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك
TABRISI:21:104-105/r14.claim: Another view identifies al-Zabur as books revealed after the Torah and al-Dhikr as the Torah.
TABRISI:21:104-105/r14.anchor: وثانيها: أن الزبور الكتب المنزلة بعد التوراة والذكر هو التوراة عن ابن عباس والضحاك

TABRISI:21:104-105/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-105/r15.speaker: الشعبي
TABRISI:21:104-105/r15.claim: Al-Sha‘bi says al-Zabur is David’s Psalter and al-Dhikr is Moses’ Torah.
TABRISI:21:104-105/r15.anchor: وثالثها: أن الزبور زبور داود والذكر توراة موسى عن الشعبي

TABRISI:21:104-105/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-105/r16.speaker: الشعبي
TABRISI:21:104-105/r16.claim: Al-Sha‘bi also reports that al-Dhikr means the Qur’an and that baʿd can mean before.
TABRISI:21:104-105/r16.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا أن الذكر القرآن وبعد بمعنى قبل

TABRISI:21:104-105/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:104-105/r17.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، ابن زيد
TABRISI:21:104-105/r17.claim: They interpret the earth inherited by God’s righteous servants as Paradise inherited by obedient people.
TABRISI:21:104-105/r17.anchor: قيل يعني أرض الجنة يرثها عبادي المطيعون عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وابن زيد

THALABI:v6p312/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p312/r6.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة
THALABI:v6p312/r6.claim: Al-A‘mash and Hamza read al-zubūr with a damma on zāy; other readers use the accusative form al-zabūra.
THALABI:v6p312/r6.anchor: قرأ الأعمش وحمزة: الزبور بضم الزاي، وغيرهما يقرءون بالنصب

THALABI:v6p312/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p312/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p312/r7.claim: The accusative form is a passive participle meaning ‘written’; the root means to write, as in zabara or dhabera a book.
THALABI:v6p312/r7.anchor: وهو بمعنى المزبور كالحلوب والركوب، يقال: زبرت الكتاب وذبرته إذا كتبته

THALABI:v6p312/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p312/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وابن زيد
THALABI:v6p312/r8.claim: They take the Zabur as revealed scriptures generally and the Reminder as the primordial Book kept with God.
THALABI:v6p312/r8.anchor: فقال سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وابن زيد: عنى بالزبور الكتب المنزلة وبالذكر أم الكتاب الذي عنده.

THALABI:v6p312/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p312/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v6p312/r9.claim: They identify the Reminder as the Torah and the Zabur as scriptures revealed after the Torah.
THALABI:v6p312/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك: الذكر التوراة والزبور الكتب المنزلة من بعد التوراة.

THALABI:v6p312/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p312/r10.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v6p312/r10.claim: Al-Sha‘bi identifies the Zabur as David’s Book and the Reminder as the Torah.
THALABI:v6p312/r10.anchor: وقال الشعبي: الزبور كتاب داود والذكر التوراة.

THALABI:v6p312/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p312/r11.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v6p312/r11.claim: Another view identifies the Zabur as David’s Book and the Reminder as the Qur’an, taking ‘after’ to mean ‘before.’
THALABI:v6p312/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الزبور زبور داود والذكر القرآن، وبعد بمعنى قبل

THALABI:v6p312/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p312/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p312/r12.claim: Here ‘the earth’ means the land of Paradise.
THALABI:v6p312/r12.anchor: أن الأرض يعني أرض الجنة يرثها عبادي الصالحون

THALABI:v6p312/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p312/r13.speaker: مجاهد وأبو العالية
THALABI:v6p312/r13.claim: Mujahid and Abu al-Aliya identify the righteous inheritors as Muhammad’s community, supported by believers’ praise for inheriting the land.
THALABI:v6p312/r13.anchor: يعني أمة محمد (عليه السلام) قاله مجاهد وأبو العالية، ودليل هذا التأويل قوله وقالوا الحمد لله

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p289/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p289/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p289/r1.claim: One interpretation identifies the inherited land as the land of Paradise.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p289/r1.anchor: يقال: أرض الجنة، ويقال: الأرض المقدسة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p289/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p289/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p289/r2.claim: Another interpretation identifies it as the Holy Land, inherited by the community of Muḥammad.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p289/r2.anchor: ويقال: الأرض المقدسة، ترثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وعلى آله.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd take the Zabur as all revealed books and the Reminder as the heavenly Mother of the Book; Abu Ishaq agrees, and the author prefers this inclusive view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r4.anchor: هذا قول سعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، وابن زيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq includes the Torah, Gospel, and Quran among the books called Zabur; zabur and book share a sense, from the verb meaning to write.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r5.anchor: قال: الزبور جميع الكتب: التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas in the reports of al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi says the Reminder is the Torah and the Zabur means books revealed after it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي، والضحاك، والسدي: الذكر: التوراة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r7.claim: In Ata’s transmission, Ibn Abbas, and also Amir al-Sha‘bi, identify the Zabur as David’s Zabur and the Reminder as the Torah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r7.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: يريد زبور داود من بعد التوراة. وهذا قول عامر الشعبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p226/r8.claim: The preferred reading is that God decreed and recorded His ruling in the books after the Mother of the Book.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p227/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p227/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p227/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas in Ata’s report, Mujahid, al-Suddi, Abu Salih, Abu al-Aliya, Said ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Zayd say the earth means Paradise; the righteous are believers who obey God, as supported by 39:74.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p227/r1.anchor: قاله ابن عباس -في رواية عطاء- ومجاهد والسدي، وأبو صالح، وأبو العالية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p227/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p227/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p227/r2.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the earthly world will pass to this community’s believers, as God manifests the religion and conquers the unbelievers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p227/r2.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: يعني الدنيا تصير للمؤمنين من هذه الأمة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r1.claim: Zabūr means something written, from zabara al-kitāb, to write it; its faʿūl pattern has passive meaning, like jalūb and rakūb for majlūb and markūb.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r1.anchor: و (الزبور) هو بمعنى مكتوب من زبر الكتاب يزبره إذا كتبه وهو فعول بمعنى مفعول، كما يقال: جلوب وركوب

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r2.claim: Kataba al-kitāb means to gather its letters, as in katb al-kharaz, gathering beads in a row.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r2.anchor: أي جمع حروفه. ومنه كتب الخرز

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r3.claim: Katabtu al-baghla describes joining the mare's two lips with a ring, another usage based on joining.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37/r3.anchor: ومنه يقال: كتبت البغلة: إذا جمعت بين شفريها بحلقة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses al-Zabur as the books, including Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an, and al-dhikr as the heavenly register, the Mother of the Book.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r3.anchor: تفسير مجاهد: يعني بالزبور الكتب، التوراة، والإنجيل، والقرآن

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r4.claim: Mujahid's interpretation identifies the earth promised to the righteous as Paradise.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the Zabur as David's Psalms, the Reminder as the Torah, and the inheriting righteous servants as Muhammad's community.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p349#2/r5.anchor: وفي تفسير ابن عباس: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور} [الأنبياء: 105] يعني زبور داود

ELMALILI:21:105/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r1.claim: He reads “after the Reminder” either as after the Torah or after earlier notices on this subject.
ELMALILI:21:105/r1.anchor: Tevrat’tan sonra Zebur’da, yahut bu babda bazı ihtârâttan sonra Zebur’da yazdık

ELMALILI:21:105/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r2.claim: God takes the earth from corrupters and gives it to rightful servants fit to inherit it and exercise stewardship.
ELMALILI:21:105/r2.anchor: Arz ifsad edenlerden alınır, verâsete lâyık, hilâfete ehil salâhiyetli hak kullarına verilir.

ELMALILI:21:105/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r3.claim: The law of righteousness governs lasting survival; the corrupt have no rightful claim to endure.
ELMALILI:21:105/r3.anchor: sırr-ı bekā, salâh kanununa müterettibdir, bozukların hakk-ı bekāsı yoktur.

ELMALILI:21:105/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r4.claim: The drowning of Pharaoh and despots, Israel inheriting the Holy Land, and David's defeat of Goliath practically foreshadowed this law; David's appointment as caliph is linked to 38:26.
ELMALILI:21:105/r4.anchor: Firavun ve cebâbirenin gark ve def‘iyle onların zayıf gördükleri kulların Arz-ı Mukaddes’in şark u garbına vâris kılınması

ELMALILI:21:105/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r5.claim: Under the law of the most righteous or most fitting, scriptural peoples first prevailed over others, then Jews, Christians, and Muslims successively prevailed; Muslims will continue while preserving righteousness.
ELMALILI:21:105/r5.anchor: Aslah kanunu” yahut “elyak kanunu” denilen bu kanunun hükmüyledir ki evvelâ sûret-i umûmiyede

ELMALILI:21:105/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r6.claim: After Muhammad's mission, inheritance belongs to one community of monotheistic believers who do righteous deeds, resist shirk, division, rebellion, and discord, and strive for the best works.
ELMALILI:21:105/r6.anchor: îmân-ı tevhid ile mü’min ve a‘mâl-i sâliha ile âmil ümmet-i vâhide olarak

ELMALILI:21:105/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r7.claim: After the heavens are folded and the earth changed, the righteous will inherit the earth of Paradise as well.
ELMALILI:21:105/r7.anchor: Nihâyet gökler dürülüp Arz değiştikten sonra arz-ı cennetin verâseti de bunlarındır.

ELMALILI:21:105/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r8.claim: Though schisms divide the Muslim community and lands are lost, a saved group following the Prophet and Companions remains, as signaled by 23:53 and sound hadith.
ELMALILI:21:105/r8.anchor: وَتَقَطَّعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ ile işaret edildiği ve ehâdîs-i sahîhada vârid olduğu üzere

ELMALILI:21:105/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r9.claim: Hadith reports that religion will become strange and the righteous strangers, then religion will reappear as it first began.
ELMALILI:21:105/r9.anchor: zamanlar gelecek din garip olacak, sâlihîn garip kalacak, sonra yine din bed’ ettiği gibi dönüp zuhur edecek

ELMALILI:21:105/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r10.claim: After about thirty false claimants to prophethood, the great Dajjal will claim divinity and perish at the Messiah's descent.
ELMALILI:21:105/r10.anchor: peygamberlik iddiasında bulunacak olan otuz kadar deccalden sonra ulûhiyet iddiasına kalkışacak olan koca Deccal, Mesih’in nüzûlüyle helâk olacak

ELMALILI:21:105/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r11.claim: Gog and Magog will bring unprecedented corruption and unimaginable wars before being destroyed by God's command.
ELMALILI:21:105/r11.anchor: Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc çıkacak, yeryüzünde görülmedik fesatlar, tasvîre sığmaz harpler yaptıktan sonra bi-emrillah mahvolacaklar

ELMALILI:21:105/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r12.claim: After the cross is broken and swine killed, the righteous will rule, Muhammad's law will be universal, and humanity will enter an age of bliss.
ELMALILI:21:105/r12.anchor: salîb kırılacak, hınzır öldürülecek, sâlihîn hâkim olacak, şer‘-i Muhammedînin ta‘mîmiyle beşeriyet bir devr-i saadete girecek

ELMALILI:21:105/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:105/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:105/r13.claim: After lesser and intermediate upheavals, the Beast, sunrise from the west, and trumpet herald the Great Resurrection; a second blast restores creation, followed by gathering, Judgment, and Paradise for the righteous.
ELMALILI:21:105/r13.anchor: Dâbbetü’larz’ın hurûcu ve Güneş’in mağribden tulû‘u ve Sûr’un nefhiyle büyük kıyamet kopacak

ELMALILI:v1p104/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p104/r1.claim: The Qur’an is called al-Hudā because it is described as guidance for people and for believers.
ELMALILI:v1p104/r1.anchor: olduğu için bir de “el-Hüdâ” tesmiye edilir.

ELMALILI:v1p104/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p104/r2.claim: Because it illuminates hearts and thoughts, the Qur’an is also named al-Nūr; 7:157 is cited.
ELMALILI:v1p104/r2.anchor: kalbleri, fikirleri tenvîr etmesi itibariyle bir ismi de “en-Nûr”dur.

ELMALILI:v1p104/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p104/r3.claim: Dhikr is a verbal noun meaning remembering or remembrance, and can also mean the thing remembered.
ELMALILI:v1p104/r3.anchor: “Zikr” dahi esasen masdar olup anmak, anış ve anılan şey mânalarını dahi ifade eder.

ELMALILI:v1p104/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p104/r4.claim: Remembering may take place in the heart or on the tongue.
ELMALILI:v1p104/r4.anchor: Anmak da ya kalb veya lisan ile olur.

ELMALILI:v1p104/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r5.speaker: Râgıb ve Kāmûs sâhibi
ELMALILI:v1p104/r5.claim: Raghib in al-Mufradat and the author of al-Qamus in Basa’ir describe dhikr as the inner state by which a person preserves acquired knowledge.
ELMALILI:v1p104/r5.anchor: Râgıb’ın[^6] Müfredât’ta[^7] ve Kāmûs sâhibinin[^8] Besâir’de beyan ettikleri üzere “zikr” maddesiyle

ELMALILI:v1p104/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p104/r6.claim: In that sense dhikr is synonymous with hifz, but hifz secures something in the heart whereas dhikr recalls it into awareness.
ELMALILI:v1p104/r6.anchor: Lâkin hıfz kalbde ihrâzı ve zikri

ELMALILI:v1p104/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p104/r7.claim: Dhikr can also mean a thing’s being present to the heart or to speech.
ELMALILI:v1p104/r7.anchor: Bazen de zikr bir şeyin kalbe veyahut

ELMALILI:v1p104/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p104/r8.claim: There is heart remembrance and tongue remembrance; each can be recalling after forgetting or continuing to remember without ever forgetting.

ELMALILI:v1p104/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p104/r9.claim: Dhikr also means name and fame, praise and commendation, and honor or status; it is used for prayer and supplication.
ELMALILI:v1p104/r9.anchor: Sonra zikir, nâm ve şöhret, medh u senâ, şeref ü şân mânalarına gelir. Namaza ve duâya ıtlak edilir.

ELMALILI:v1p104/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p104/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p104/r10.claim: Dhikr can refer to heavenly books that set out religion and law and establish the community’s rulings; 54:25 and 21:105 illustrate this sense.
ELMALILI:v1p104/r10.anchor: Bir de zikr, din ve şerî‘atı tafsîl ve ahkâm-ı milleti vaz‘eden semâvî kitaplara denir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r1.claim: The preferred reading takes “remembrance” as the Torah given to Moses, “Psalms” as David’s book, and “earth” as the world generally or the particular place connected with the account.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r1.anchor: Bizim de tercih ettiğimiz görüşe göre zikir kelimesi Hz. Mûsâ’ya indirilen Tevrat’ı, Zebûr Hz. Dâvûd’a indirilen kitabı, arz da genel olarak yeryüzünü

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r2.claim: On this reading, God announces in those books and the Qur’an that evil cannot endure, goodness is fundamental and evil incidental, and the good are destined ultimately to rule.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r2.anchor: adı geçen kitaplarda ve Kur’an’da, dünyada kötülerin ve kötülüğün sürekli olarak pâyidar olamayacağını; iyiliğin asıl, kötülüğün ise ârızî olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r3.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r3.claim: One alternative reads “Psalms” as David’s book, “remembrance” as the Torah, and “earth” as the world or a region of struggle.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r3.anchor: a) “Zebûr”, Hz. Dâvûd’a vahyedilen kitap, “zikir”, Tevrat ve “arz” da dünya veya mücadele bölgesi olan yerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r4.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r4.claim: Another alternative takes “Psalms” as all revealed books, “remembrance” as warnings in revelation or the Preserved Tablet, and “earth” as Paradise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r4.anchor: b) “Zebûr” bütün peygamberlere gönderilen küçüklü büyüklü kitaplar, “zikir” vahyedilen kitaplarda yapılan uyarılar veya levh-i mahfuz, “arz” da cennettir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r5.claim: The promise that the good inherit the earth is expressed in nearly the same words in the Psalms attributed to David.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r5.anchor: 105. âyetteki “Yeryüzü iyi kullarıma kalacaktır” ifadesi, Hz. Dâvûd’a nisbet edilen Mezmurlar’da da hemen aynı şekilde yer almaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r6.claim: “Ṣāliḥ” means good, proper, sound, virtuous, or fitting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r6.anchor: “İyi” diye tercüme edilen salih kelimesi, “iyi, düzgün, sağlam, erdemli, uygun” mânasına gelmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r7.claim: One reading sees historical worldly inheritance: the righteous do not always rule, but ultimately prevail and inherit wealth and authority; prophetic communities survive while tyrants and opponents fall.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r7.anchor: Genel olarak tarihte olup bitenlere bakıldığında her zaman iyilerin (sâlih kulların) hâkim olduklarını söylemek mümkün değilse de, eninde sonunda onların kazandığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r8.claim: The commentary illustrates this historical pattern with the Prophet’s persecutors, who were ultimately defeated and whose property and lands passed to Muslims.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r8.anchor: İslâm tarihinde de Hz. Peygamber’e karşı çıkan ve ona her türlü zulmü ve baskıyı uygulayan inkârcılar sonunda mağlûp ve perişan olmuşlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r9.claim: A second reading concerns the end times, when God empowers servants to reform the world and establish order, peace, justice, and fair distribution.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r9.anchor: Kıyamet yaklaşınca Allah Teâlâ dünyayı ıslah etmek, yeryüzünde düzeni, huzuru, adaleti ve âdil paylaşımı hâkim kılmak için bazı kullarına görev ve imkân verecek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r10.claim: A third reading takes the earth as the afterlife replacing this transient world: the righteous, meaning good and virtuous people by God’s standard, inherit Paradise and both worlds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:105/r10.anchor: Bu fâni dünyanın (arz) yerine gelecek (vârisi olacak) olan öteki dünyadır (âhiretteki arzdır), öteki dünyanın ebedî mutluluk alanının adı cennettir

BURHAN:v1p275/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p275/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p275/r1.claim: The Qur'an is designated by many names and descriptions, including criterion, faith, command, glad tidings, majestic, Zabur, clear, herald and warner, mighty, message, and stories; one verse gives four names for the scrolls.
BURHAN:v1p275/r1.anchor: وسماه زبورا فقال ﴿ ولقد كتبنا في الزبور ﴾ الآية

ITQAN:v1p146#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p146#2/r1.speaker: كعب
ITQAN:v1p146#2/r1.claim: Kaʿb reports a Torah passage addressed to Muḥammad that calls the revelation sent to him a new Torah, which opens blind eyes, deaf ears and closed hearts.
ITQAN:v1p146#2/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن الضريس وغيره عن كعب قال في التوراة يا محمد إني منزل عليك توراة حديثة تفتح أعينا عميا

ITQAN:v1p146#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p146#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ITQAN:v1p146#2/r2.claim: Qatāda reports Moses asking that the people whose gospels are in their hearts, described in the tablets, be made his community; God says they are Aḥmad's community.
ITQAN:v1p146#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال لما أخذ موسى الألواح قال يا رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة أناجيلهم في قلوبهم

ITQAN:v1p146#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p146#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p146#2/r3.claim: The reports call the Qur'an Torah and Gospel, but the author says those names may not be applied to it now; he compares this with Torah called Furqān and the Psalms called Qur'an, citing 2:53.
ITQAN:v1p146#2/r3.anchor: ففي هذين الأثرين تسمية القرآن توراة وإنجيلا ومع هذا لا يجوز الآن أن يطلق عليه ذلك

ITQAN:v1p158/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p158/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p158/r1.claim: A report from Wāthila b. al-Asqaʿ says the Prophet received the seven long suras in place of Torah, the hundred-verse suras for Psalms, the mathānī for Gospel, and the mufassal as an added gift.
ITQAN:v1p158/r1.anchor: من حديث واثلة بن الأسقع أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أعطيت مكان التوراة السبع الطول وأعطيت مكان الزبور المئين

ITQAN:v1p158/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p158/r2.speaker: بعض السلف
ITQAN:v1p158/r2.claim: Some early Muslims used figurative names for sura groupings: fields, gardens, chambers, brides, brocades and meadows, alongside names such as the ṭawāsīm and ḥawāmīm.
ITQAN:v1p158/r2.anchor: قال بعض السلف في القرآن ميادين وبساتين ومقاصير وعرائس وديابيح ورياض

ITQAN:v1p158/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p158/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p158/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd calls the ḥawāmīm the Qur'an's brocade.
ITQAN:v1p158/r3.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم عن ابن مسعود قال الحواميم ديباج القرآن

ITQAN:v1p158/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p158/r4.speaker: السخاوي
ITQAN:v1p158/r4.claim: Al-Sakhāwī explains that the Qur'an's qawāriʿ are protective verses, named because they strike, repel and subdue Satan; examples include the Throne Verse and the two refuge suras.
ITQAN:v1p158/r4.anchor: قال السخاوي وقوارع القرآن الآيات التي يتعوذ بها ويتحصن سميت بذلك لأنها تقرع الشيطان

ITQAN:v1p158/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p158/r5.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
ITQAN:v1p158/r5.claim: A marfūʿ report from Muʿādh b. Anas calls the verse beginning الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا the Verse of Might.
ITQAN:v1p158/r5.anchor: وفي مسند أحمد من حديث معاذ بن أنس مرفوعا آية العز

ITQAN:v1p179#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r1.claim: Sura divisions make each sura an independent miracle with a distinct subject; dividing the Qur'an into long, middle and short suras shows that length is not required for inimitability and helps teach children progressively.
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r1.anchor: الحكمة في تسوير القرآن سورا تحقيق كون السورة بمجردها معجزة وآية من آيات الله والإشارة إلى أن كل سورة نمط مستقل

ITQAN:v1p179#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r2.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r2.claim: Al-Zarkashī says earlier scriptures were not divided into suras because their arrangement was not miraculous and they were not made easy to memorize.
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r2.anchor: قال الزركشي في البرهان فإن قلت فهلا كانت الكتب السالفة كذلك قلت لوجهين أحدهما أنها لم تكن معجزات من جهة النظم والترتيب

ITQAN:v1p179#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says earlier scriptures were also divided into suras; divisions vary subject matter, motivate readers at each finish, make memorized portions feel complete, and align similar forms and meanings.
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r3.anchor: الفائدة في تفصيل القرآن وتقطيعه سورا كثيرة وكذلك أنزل الله التوراة والإنجيل والزبور

ITQAN:v1p179#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r4.claim: The author prefers al-Zamakhsharī's claim that earlier scriptures were divided into suras and calls it correct or more nearly correct.
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r4.anchor: وما ذكره الزمخشري من تسوير سائر الكتب هو الصحيح أو الصواب

ITQAN:v1p179#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says the Psalms had 150 suras of exhortation and praise, without rules of lawful or forbidden acts, duties or limits; they also spoke of a Gospel sura called Proverbs.
ITQAN:v1p179#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قال كنا نتحدث أن الزبور مائة وخمسون سورة كلها مواعظ وثناء ليس فيه حلال ولا حرام

ITQAN:v2p420/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p420/r3.speaker: ابن خالويه
ITQAN:v2p420/r3.claim: Ibn Khālawayh says the only Qur'anic بعد meaning before is in the phrase after the Reminder in 21:105.
ITQAN:v2p420/r3.anchor: وقال ابن خالويه ليس في القرآن بعد بمعنى قبل إلا حرف واحد

ITQAN:v2p420/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p420/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v2p420/r6.claim: A report from the Prophet says every Qur'anic use of qunūt means obedience; its chain is good and Ibn Ḥibbān authenticates it.
ITQAN:v2p420/r6.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال كل حرف في القرآن يذكر فيه القنوت فهو الطاعة هذا إسناده جيد وابن حبان يصححه

ITQAN:v2p420/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p420/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p420/r7.claim: ʿIkrima reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that every Qur'anic use of alīm means painful.
ITQAN:v2p420/r7.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال كل شيء في القرآن أليم فهو الموجع

ITQAN:v2p420/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p420/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p420/r8.claim: ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭalḥa reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that every Qur'anic use of qatl means cursing.
ITQAN:v2p420/r8.anchor: من طريق علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال كل شيء في القرآن قتل فهو لعن

ITQAN:v2p420/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p420/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p420/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that Qur'anic rijz means punishment.
ITQAN:v2p420/r9.anchor: من طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال كل شيء في كتاب الله من الرجز يعني به العذاب

ITQAN:v2p420/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p420/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p420/r10.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that every Qur'anic tasbīḥ means prayer and every sulṭān means proof.
ITQAN:v2p420/r10.anchor: حدثنا قيس عن عمار الدهني عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال كل تسبيح في القرآن صلاة وكل سلطان في القرآن حجة

ITQAN:v2p420/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p420/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p420/r11.claim: ʿIkrima reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that every Qur'anic use of dīn means reckoning.
ITQAN:v2p420/r11.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال كل شيء في القرآن الدين فهو الحساب

ITQAN:v2p420/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p420/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p420/r12.claim: Al-Suddī reports from Abū Mālik from Ibn ʿAbbās that rayb means doubt except in ريب المنون, where it means events of fate.
ITQAN:v2p420/r12.anchor: من طريق السدي عن أبي مالك عن ابن عباس قال كل ريب شك إلا مكانا واحدا في الطور

ITQAN:v4p415/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p415/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p415/r1.claim: The Prophet tells ʿUqba that no suras like al-Ikhlāṣ and the two refuge suras were revealed in Torah, Psalms, Gospel or Qur'an.
ITQAN:v4p415/r1.anchor: أخرج أحمد من حديث عقبة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له

ITQAN:v4p415/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p415/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p415/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet naming al-Falaq and al-Nās as the best refuge recited by those seeking protection.
ITQAN:v4p415/r2.anchor: وأخرج أيضا من حديث ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له

ITQAN:v4p415/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p415/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p415/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Khubayb reports the Prophet's instruction to recite al-Ikhlāṣ and the two refuge suras three times in the morning and evening; they suffice against everything.
ITQAN:v4p415/r3.anchor: وأخرج أبو داود والترمذي عن عبد الله بن خبيب قال قال رسول الله

ITQAN:v4p415/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p415/r4.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v4p415/r4.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha says reciting al-Ikhlāṣ and the two refuge suras seven times after Friday prayer brings protection from harm until the next Friday.
ITQAN:v4p415/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن السني من حديث عائشة ( من قرأ بعد صلاة الجمعة

DAMGHANI:v1p28/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p28/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p28/r3.claim: In 21:105, الأرض means Paradise; the inheritance language in 39:74 likewise refers to inheriting Paradise.
DAMGHANI:v1p28/r3.anchor: فوجه منها : الأرض يعني الجنة . قوله سبحانه في سورة الأنبياء

DAMGHANI:v1p28/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p28/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p28/r6.claim: Damghani's thirteen referents for أرض also include Mecca, Egypt, Islamic lands, the whole earth, the grave, wilderness, resurrection land, heart, mosque courtyard, and foreground.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p305/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p305/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p305/r3.claim: The eighteenth sense is the Preserved Tablet.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p305/r3.anchor: والثامن عشر : اللوح المحفوظ . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنبياء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p305/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p305/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p305/r4.claim: Some say al-zabūr in this verse means all the earlier books.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p305/r4.anchor: وقيل : أراد بالزبور ها هنا سائر الكتب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r1.claim: Zubūr is the plural of zabūr, a book; al-Zajjaj says a zabūr is any book containing wisdom. Zabartu al-kitāb means ‘I wrote the book.’
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r1.anchor: الزبر : جمع زبور . والزبور : الكتاب . وقال الزجاج : الزبور كل كتاب ذو حكمة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r2.claim: The related forms also mean chest, a piece of iron, a calamity, rebuking someone, and one’s writing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r2.anchor: والزبرة : الصدرة - وزبرة الحديد : قطعة منه . والزبير : الداهية . وزبرت الرجل : انتهرته

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r5.claim: The third sense is David’s Psalter, named alongside God’s writing about the righteous inheriting the earth.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r5.anchor: والثالث : كتاب داود . ومنه قوله تعالى ( 66 / ب ) في الأنبياء

BURHAN:v1p280/r18.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r18.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r18.claim: In the cited verse, al-Zabur means all revealed books, not only David's Psalms; al-dhikr means the Mother of the Book from God.
BURHAN:v1p280/r18.anchor: فالمراد بالزبور هنا جميع الكتب المنزلة من السماء لا يختص بزبور داود والذكر أم الكتاب الذى من عند الله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p279/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p279/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p279/r11.claim: The phrase about the Psalms after the Reminder is cited on the interpretation that al-dhikr here means the Qur'an.
BURHAN:v3p279/r11.anchor: على قول من يقول إن الذكر هنا القرآن

DAMGHANI:v1p182/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r3.claim: Dhikr can mean the Preserved Tablet.
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r3.anchor: " ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر " يعني اللوح المحفوظ

NASHR:v2p252/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p252/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p252/r8.claim: For زبورا here and الزبور in al-Israʾ and al-Anbiyaʾ, Hamza and Khalaf use ḍamma on zāy while the others use fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p252/r8.anchor: فقرأ حمزة وخلف بضم الزاي، وقرأ الباقون بفتحها

NASHR:v2p170/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p170/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p170/r1.claim: Across fourteen disputed yāʾs before hamzat waṣl plus the definite article, Ḥamza alone sukunizes every yāʾ.
NASHR:v2p170/r1.anchor: والمختلف فيه من ذلك أربع عشرة ياء: في البقرة ثنتان لا ينال عهدي الظالمين،

NASHR:v2p170/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p170/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p170/r5.claim: The readers agree to fatḥa on the remaining eighteen yāʾs in this section.
NASHR:v2p170/r5.anchor: على فتح ما بقي من هذا الفصل، وهو ثماني عشرة ياء
